HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.\n- hyperframes-audio: Use when audio already placed in a HyperFrames composition needs to be mixed: fade-in/fade-out, crossfade, track gain or volume, volume automation, ducking, a music bed that fights a voiceover (voiceover carve), effects on a track (EQ, compressor, limiter, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, chorus, phaser, bitcrush), automation envelopes drawn on a track's volume or any effect parameter, or one submix bus carrying a chain, a fader and an automation clock for several tracks at once (`&lt;hf-audio-group&gt;`). Don't use for sourcing or generating audio — finding BGM, SFX, or making a voiceover is `/media-use`. Don't use for clip timing or track layout, which is `/hyperframes-core`.\n- hyperframes-cli: Use the HyperFrames CLI development loop: init, add, catalog, capture, lint, check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare, preview, play, present, beats, keyframes, single or batch render, publish, cloud, cloudrun, feedback, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, timeline, history, clean, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, auth, tts, and remove-background. Also use when diagnosing build or render failures. validate, inspect, and layout are deprecated aliases; use check. Covers local, HeyGen-hosted cloud, AWS Lambda, and Google Cloud Run rendering.\n- hyperframes-core: The HyperFrames composition contract — build one renderable project. Use for composition structure, the `data-*` timing attributes, `class=\"clip\"`, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, framework-owned media playback, deterministic-render rules, and validation. Read before writing composition HTML.\n- hyperframes-creative: Non-animation creative direction for HyperFrames videos. Use for design spec (frame.md / design.md) handling, palettes, typography, narration, beat planning, audio-reactive visuals, composition patterns, and brand / style decisions. For atomic motion patterns and scene blueprints, use `hyperframes-animation`.\n- hyperframes-keyframes: Use when a HyperFrames composition needs a punch-in, punch-out, zoom, reframe, Ken Burns treatment, camera move, visual match/whip handoff, or other seek-safe 2D/3D keyframes; also for GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, paths, masks, SVG morph/draw, text trails, 3D depth, or `hyperframes keyframes` diagnostics. Don't use for broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.\n- hyperframes-registry: Search, install, and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use BEFORE hand-building any named visual — whenever a brief, a user, or a storyboard names a look, effect, treatment, or transition such as CRT scanlines, glitch, chromatic aberration, film grain, a shimmer sweep, a chart, a code or terminal window, a map, or a confetti burst — because roughly 400 hosted items already cover many of them and the search ranks all of them with nothing installed, no project, and no account. Also use when running hyperframes add or hyperframes catalog, installing one item or every block matching a tag, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers discovery, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and authoring a new block or component to contribute upstream (idea → scaffold → validate → PR).\n- hyperframes-studio: Use when working with a person on a HyperFrames project in Studio: first, whether their message asks for a change at all (questions, loose ideas and \"don't change anything\" get an answer and a plan, not an edit); for a new film, the plan, storyboard and build order that the HyperFrames launch films follow; and how the timeline should be laid out so it reads well (one caption track, one element kind per track, every scene a sub-composition) and where captions and key content may sit (safe zones). Don't use for how to perform an individual edit (split, trim, retime, volume, copy, swap): that is `creator-editing-recipes.md` in `/hyperframes-core`.\n- implementing-react-i18n: Use for React translations, locale resources, language selectors, or stale UI after locale changes\n- improve: Survey any codebase as a senior advisor and produce prioritized, self-contained implementation plans for OTHER models/agents to execute. Strictly read-only on source code — never implements, fixes, or refactors anything itself. Use when asked to audit a codebase, find improvement opportunities (bugs, security, performance, test coverage, tech debt, migrations, DX), suggest features or where to take the project next (roadmap, product direction), or generate handoff plans for another agent to implement.\n- instrumenting-control-planes: Use for observable backend or agent workflows, long-running jobs, retries, recovery, and user-visible failures\n- learning-from-bugs: Use for requested postmortems or reusable lessons from serious architecture, data, security, recovery, or operational failures\n- media-use: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal.\n- optimizing-react-next-apps: Use to improve React or Next.js load, compile, render, hydration, bundle, import, or dependency performance\n- receiving-code-review: Use to apply code-review feedback, especially when it is unclear, conflicting, or scope-expanding\n- requesting-code-review: Use when the user requests code review or substantial, high-risk work needs independent review\n- second-opinion: Use only when the user explicitly asks to write an implementation plan to a file\n- start-from-blocks: Use before planning or building a new web-app screen, form, dashboard, or major UI section\n- subagent-driven-development: Use to execute a written plan whose substantial tasks justify delegated implementation\n- systematic-debugging: Use to find the cause of a bug, test failure, slowdown, or unexpected result\n- talking-head-recut: Package an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video with timed, designed GRAPHIC OVERLAY cards — kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, quotes, side panels, picture-in-picture — synced to the transcript, on a 16:9 / 9:16 / 4:5 canvas of your choice; the clip plays untouched underneath. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes.       {
        "name": "Bash",
        "description": "Executes a bash command and returns its output.\n\n- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.\n- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.\n- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.\n- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.\n- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.\n\n# Git\n- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.\n- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).\n- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.\n- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.\n- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.",

              "description": "Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "description": {
              "description": "Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like \"complex\" or \"risk\" in the description - just describe what it does.\n\nSay what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.\n\nFor simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):\n- ls → \"List files in current directory\"\n- git status → \"Show working tree status\"\n- npm install → \"Install package dependencies\"\n\nFor commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:\n- find . -name \"*.tmp\" -exec rm {} \\; → \"Find and delete all .tmp files recursively\"\n- git reset --hard origin/main → \"Discard all local changes and match remote main\"\n- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → \"Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements\"",

              "type": "boolean"

          "additionalProperties": false
        },
        "eager_input_streaming": true

      {
        "name": "ScheduleWakeup",
        "description": "Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.\n\nDo NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.\n\nPass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.\n\nSet `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report (\"no change\", \"still waiting\", \"quiet hold\"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).\n\n## Picking delaySeconds\n\nThis session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)\n\nMatch the delay to what you're actually waiting for:\n\n- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.\n- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.\n- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.\n\nDon't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.\n\n## The reason field\n\nOne short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. \"watching CI run\" beats \"waiting.\" The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.\n",
        "input_schema": {
          "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "delaySeconds": {
              "description": "Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "reason": {
              "description": "One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "prompt": {
              "description": "The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "stop": {
              "description": "Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "noop": {
              "description": "true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.",
              "type": "boolean"
            }
          },
          "additionalProperties": false
        },
        "eager_input_streaming": true
      },
      {
        "name": "Skill",
        "description": "Invoke a skill.\n\nA skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or \"slash command\"); that's a request to invoke it.\n\n- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).\n- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.\n\nOnly names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.\n",

      {
        "name": "Workflow",
        "description": "Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.\n\nONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:\n- The user included the keyword \"ultracode\" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).\n- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.\n- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words (\"use a workflow\", \"run a workflow\", \"fan out agents\", \"orchestrate this with subagents\"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.\n- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.\n- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.\n\nFor any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with \"use a workflow\" in a future message to skip the ask.\n\nEvery script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.\n\nThe canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:\n  export const meta = {\n    name: 'review-changes',\n    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',\n    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],\n  }\n  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]\n  const results = await pipeline(\n    DIMENSIONS,\n    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),\n    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>\n      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})\n        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))\n    ))\n  )\n  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)\n  return { confirmed }\n  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.\n\nBefore writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.\n\nThis session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with \"Dynamic workflow size\" in /config.",

          "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

          "properties": {
            "script": {
              "description": "Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().",
              "type": "string",
              "maxLength": 524288
            },

            },
            "title": {

              "type": "string"
            },
            "args": {

Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question)."
            },
            "scriptPath": {
              "description": "Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "resumeFromRunId": {

              "type": "string",

            }
          },
          "additionalProperties": false

        "eager_input_streaming": true

        "name": "Write",
        "description": "Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.\n\nWhen to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.",
        "input_schema": {

377	
378	              {group.path !== "other" ? (
379	                <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-0.5">

382	                    size="icon"

384	                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.newConversationInProject", { project: group.name })}
385	                    onClick={() => beginConversationInProject(group.path)}

387	                    <Plus className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
388	                  </Button>
389	                  <DropdownMenu>

503	                              ) : null}
504	                            </span>

523	                                  if (event.key === "Enter") {

531	                                onBlur={() => commitRenamingRun(run.id)}
532	                                autoFocus

534	                              />
535	                            ) : (

538	                          </div>

562	                                aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.conversationActions", { title: run.title })}
563	                              >
564	                                <MoreHorizontal className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
565	                              </DropdownMenuTrigger>
566	                              <DropdownMenuContent align="end" className="min-w-28">
567	                                <DropdownMenuItem
568	                                  className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
569	                                  onClick={(event) => {
570	                                    event.stopPropagation();
571	                                    startRenamingRun(run);
572	                                  }}
573	                                >
574	                                  <Pencil className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.rename")}
575	                                </DropdownMenuItem>
576	                                {canMoveConversation ? (
577	                                  <DropdownMenuItem
578	                                    className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
579	                                    onClick={(event) => {
580	                                      event.stopPropagation();
581	                                      startMovingRun(run);
582	                                    }}
583	                                  >
584	                                    <FolderInput className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.moveToProject")}
585	                                  </DropdownMenuItem>
586	                                ) : null}
587	                                {canArchiveConversation ? (
588	                                  <DropdownMenuItem
589	                                    className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
590	                                    onClick={(event) => {
591	                                      event.stopPropagation();
592	                                      archiveRun(run);
593	                                    }}
594	                                  >
595	                                    <Archive className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.archive")}
596	                                  </DropdownMenuItem>
597	                                ) : null}
598	                                <DropdownMenuItem
599	                                  variant="destructive"
600	                                  className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
601	                                  onClick={(event) => {
602	                                    event.stopPropagation();
603	                                    deleteRun(run);
604	                                  }}
605	                                >
606	                                  <Trash2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.delete")}
607	                                </DropdownMenuItem>
608	                              </DropdownMenuContent>
609	                            </DropdownMenu>
610	                          </div>
611	                        </div>
612	                      </div>
613	                    </div>
614	                  );
615	                })}
616	                {hiddenSessionCount > 0 ? (
617	                  <button
618	                    type="button"
619	                    className="ml-7 mt-1 inline-flex h-7 items-center rounded-md px-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-muted/60 hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
620	                    aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.showMoreSessions", {
621	                      count: nextSessionBatchCount,
622	                      project: group.name,
623	                    })}
624	                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.showMoreSessions", {
625	                      count: nextSessionBatchCount,
626	                      project: group.name,
627	                    })}
628	                    onClick={() => onShowMoreProjectSessions(group.path)}
629	                  >
630	                    {t("conversation.sidebar.moreSessions")}
631	                  </button>
632	                ) : null}
633	              </div>
634	            </div>
635	          </Collapsible>
636	        );
637	      })}
638	    </>
639	  );
640	}

642	interface MoveRunToProjectDialogProps {
643	  open: boolean;
644	  moveRunProjectPath: string;
645	  moveRunToProjectOptions: string[];
646	  isMoveRunToProjectPending: boolean;
647	  setMoveRunProjectPath: (value: string) => void;
648	  confirmMoveRunToProject: () => void;

651	
652	function MoveRunToProjectDialog({
653	  open,
654	  moveRunProjectPath,
655	  moveRunToProjectOptions,
656	  isMoveRunToProjectPending,
657	  setMoveRunProjectPath,
658	  confirmMoveRunToProject,
659	  cancelMovingRun,
660	}: MoveRunToProjectDialogProps) {
661	  return (
662	    <Dialog
663	      open={open}
664	      onOpenChange={(nextOpen) => {
665	        if (!nextOpen) {
666	          cancelMovingRun();
667	        }
668	      }}
669	    >
670	      <DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>
671	        <DialogHeader>
672	          <DialogTitle>{t("conversation.moveProject.title")}</DialogTitle>
673	          <DialogDescription>
674	            {moveRunToProjectOptions.length > 0
675	              ? t("conversation.moveProject.description")
676	              : t("conversation.moveProject.empty")}
677	          </DialogDescription>
678	        </DialogHeader>
679	        <div className="grid gap-2">
680	          <label className="text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground" htmlFor="move-run-project-select">
681	            {t("conversation.moveProject.projectLabel")}
682	          </label>
683	          <select
684	            id="move-run-project-select"
685	            className="h-9 w-full rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm text-foreground shadow-xs outline-none transition-colors focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60"
686	            value={moveRunProjectPath}
687	            onChange={(event) => setMoveRunProjectPath(event.target.value)}
688	            disabled={isMoveRunToProjectPending || moveRunToProjectOptions.length === 0}
689	          >
690	            <option value="">{t("conversation.moveProject.placeholder")}</option>
691	            {moveRunToProjectOptions.map((projectPath) => (
692	              <option key={projectPath} value={projectPath}>
693	                {projectPath}
694	              </option>
695	            ))}
696	          </select>
697	        </div>
698	        <DialogFooter>
699	          <Button
700	            type="button"
701	            variant="outline"
702	            onClick={cancelMovingRun}
703	            disabled={isMoveRunToProjectPending}
704	          >
705	            {t("common.cancel")}
706	          </Button>
707	          <Button
708	            type="button"
709	            onClick={confirmMoveRunToProject}
710	            disabled={!moveRunProjectPath || isMoveRunToProjectPending}
711	          >
712	            {t("conversation.moveProject.ok")}
713	          </Button>
714	        </DialogFooter>
715	      </DialogContent>
716	    </Dialog>
717	  );
718	}

720	export interface ConversationSidebarProps {
721	  filteredProjects: SidebarGroup[];
722	  activeProjects: SidebarGroup[];
723	  conversationSidebarTab: ConversationSidebarTab;
724	  setConversationSidebarTab: (tab: ConversationSidebarTab) => void;
725	  isHydratingConversations: boolean;
726	  searchQuery: string;
727	  setSearchQuery: (value: string) => void;
728	  selectedRunId: string | null;
729	  messages: Array<{ runId: string; role?: string | null; kind?: string | null; content?: string | null; createdAt: string }> | undefined;
730	  readMarkers: Record<string, string>;
731	  collapsedProjectPaths: Set<string>;
732	  visibleProjectSessionCounts: Record<string, number>;

734	  onReorderProjects: (draggedPath: string, targetPath: string, placement: ProjectDropPlacement) => void;
735	  onCollapseAllProjects: (projectPaths: string[]) => void;
736	  onShowMoreProjectSessions: (projectPath: string) => void;

738	  openOnboarding: () => void;

740	  startNewPlan: () => void;
741	  beginConversationInProject: (projectPath: string) => void;
742	  presetCommands: ProjectPresetCommandMenuItem[];
743	  runPresetCommand: (projectPath: string, presetCommandId: string) => void;
744	  isPresetCommandPending: boolean;
745	  handleRemoveProject: (pathToRemove: string) => void;
746	  selectRun: (runId: string) => void;
747	  renamingRunId: string | null;
748	  renameValue: string;
749	  renameSource: "sidebar" | "topbar" | null;
750	  setRenameValue: (value: string) => void;
751	  movingRunId: string | null;
752	  moveRunProjectPath: string;
753	  moveRunToProjectOptions: string[];
754	  setMoveRunProjectPath: (value: string) => void;
755	  startMovingRun: (run: SidebarRun) => void;
756	  confirmMoveRunToProject: () => void;
757	  cancelMovingRun: () => void;
758	  isMoveRunToProjectPending: boolean;
759	  startRenamingRun: (run: SidebarRun) => void;
760	  commitRenamingRun: (runId: string) => void;
761	  cancelRenamingRun: () => void;
762	  archiveRun: (run: SidebarRun) => void;

767	  themeMode: "day" | "night";
768	  setThemeMode: React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<"day" | "night">>;
769	  onCollapse?: () => void;
770	  onOpenExternalSessions?: () => void;
771	  runnerControlsMode?: "desktop" | "mobile";

773	
774	/**
775	 * Memoized. Every SSE frame gave the shell a new state identity and re-rendered
776	 * this entire subtree, even when nothing it renders had changed. Its props are
777	 * spread from `sharedSidebarProps`, whose callbacks are now stable, so the
778	 * shallow comparison is meaningful.
779	 */
780	const ConversationSidebar = memo(function ConversationSidebar({
781	  filteredProjects,
782	  activeProjects,
783	  conversationSidebarTab,
784	  setConversationSidebarTab,
785	  isHydratingConversations,
786	  searchQuery,
787	  setSearchQuery,
788	  selectedRunId,
789	  messages,
790	  readMarkers,
791	  collapsedProjectPaths,
792	  visibleProjectSessionCounts,
793	  onProjectOpenChange,
794	  onReorderProjects,
795	  onCollapseAllProjects,
796	  onShowMoreProjectSessions,
797	  setShowSettings,
798	  openOnboarding,
799	  openFolderPicker,
800	  startNewPlan,
801	  beginConversationInProject,
802	  presetCommands,
803	  runPresetCommand,
804	  isPresetCommandPending,
805	  handleRemoveProject,
806	  selectRun,
807	  renamingRunId,
808	  renameValue,
809	  renameSource,
810	  setRenameValue,
811	  movingRunId,
812	  moveRunProjectPath,
813	  moveRunToProjectOptions,
814	  setMoveRunProjectPath,
815	  startMovingRun,
816	  confirmMoveRunToProject,
817	  cancelMovingRun,
818	  isMoveRunToProjectPending,
819	  startRenamingRun,
820	  commitRenamingRun,
821	  cancelRenamingRun,
822	  archiveRun,
823	  deleteRun,
824	  authEnabled,
825	  openPairDeviceDialog,
826	  logout,
827	  themeMode,
828	  setThemeMode,
829	  onCollapse,
830	  onOpenExternalSessions,
831	  runnerControlsMode = "desktop",
832	}: ConversationSidebarProps) {
833	  useI18nSnapshot();
834	  const themeModeLabel = t(themeMode === "night" ? "theme.mode.switchDay" : "theme.mode.switchNight");
835	  const visibleProjectGroups = conversationSidebarTab === "projects" ? filteredProjects : activeProjects;
836	  const hasExpandedVisibleProjectGroup = visibleProjectGroups.some((group) => !collapsedProjectPaths.has(group.path));
837	  const mounted = useSyncExternalStore(
838	    useCallback((listener) => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.subscribe(listener), []),
839	    useCallback(() => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.getSnapshot(), []),
840	    () => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.getSnapshot(),
841	  );
842	  const scrollAreaRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
843	  const scrollSettledRef = useRef(false);
844	  const programmaticScrollTopRef = useRef<number | null>(null);
845	  const handleSidebarPointerDown = useCallback((event: React.PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
846	    mobileConversationSwipeManager.start(event, runnerControlsMode === "mobile", "close");
847	  }, [runnerControlsMode]);
848	  const handleSidebarPointerMove = useCallback((event: React.PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
849	    mobileConversationSwipeManager.move(event);
850	  }, []);
851	  const handleSidebarPointerUp = useCallback((event: React.PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
852	    if (mobileConversationSwipeManager.finish(event) === "close") {
853	      onCollapse?.();
854	    }
855	  }, [onCollapse]);
856	  const handleSidebarPointerCancel = useCallback((event: React.PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
857	    if (mobileConversationSwipeManager.cancel(event) === "close") {
858	      onCollapse?.();
859	    }
860	  }, [onCollapse]);
861	  const sidebarContentKey = useMemo(
862	    () => visibleProjectGroups
863	      .map((group) => `${group.path}:${group.runs.map((run) => run.id).join(",")}`)
864	      .join("|"),
865	    [visibleProjectGroups],
866	  );
867	  const getScrollViewport = useCallback(
868	    () => scrollAreaRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-slot="scroll-area-viewport"]') ?? null,
869	    [],
870	  );
871	
872	  useEffect(() => {
873	    if (!mounted) {
874	      return;
875	    }
876	    const viewport = getScrollViewport();
877	    if (!viewport) {
878	      return;
879	    }
880	    const saveScrollPosition = () => {
881	      conversationSidebarScrollManager.setScrollTop(runnerControlsMode, viewport.scrollTop);
882	    };
883	    const handleScroll = () => {
884	      const programmaticScrollTop = programmaticScrollTopRef.current;
885	      if (programmaticScrollTop === null || Math.abs(viewport.scrollTop - programmaticScrollTop) > 1) {
886	        // The user is driving the list now, so pending centring attempts stop.
887	        scrollSettledRef.current = true;
888	      }
889	      saveScrollPosition();
890	    };
891	    viewport.addEventListener("scroll", handleScroll, { passive: true });
892	    return () => {
893	      saveScrollPosition();
894	      viewport.removeEventListener("scroll", handleScroll);
895	    };
896	  }, [getScrollViewport, mounted, runnerControlsMode]);
897	
898	  useLayoutEffect(() => {
899	    if (!mounted || scrollSettledRef.current) {
900	      return;
901	    }
902	    const viewport = getScrollViewport();
903	    if (!viewport) {
904	      return;
905	    }
906	    const applyScrollTop = (scrollTop: number) => {
907	      programmaticScrollTopRef.current = scrollTop;
908	      viewport.scrollTop = scrollTop;
909	    };
910	    const selectedRow = runnerControlsMode === "mobile" && selectedRunId
911	      ? findConversationRunRow(viewport, selectedRunId)
912	      : null;
913	    if (selectedRow) {
914	      // Centring outranks the remembered offset: that offset was saved when the
915	      // drawer last closed — usually right after tapping a run, with the tapped
916	      // row wherever the finger happened to land — so restoring it leaves the
917	      // current run off centre.
918	      applyScrollTop(centeredScrollTopForRow(viewport, selectedRow));
919	      scrollSettledRef.current = true;
920	      // The drawer paints a frame after mount, so anything that settles late
921	      // (runner controls, brand icons) would nudge the row off centre. One
922	      // re-measure covers that, and it backs off once the user scrolls.
923	      const frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
924	        const programmaticScrollTop = programmaticScrollTopRef.current;
925	        if (!selectedRow.isConnected || programmaticScrollTop === null) {
926	          return;
927	        }
928	        if (Math.abs(viewport.scrollTop - programmaticScrollTop) > 1) {
929	          return;
930	        }
931	        applyScrollTop(centeredScrollTopForRow(viewport, selectedRow));
932	      });
933	      return () => {
934	        cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
935	      };
936	    }
937	    const savedScrollTop = conversationSidebarScrollManager.getScrollTop(runnerControlsMode);
938	    if (savedScrollTop !== undefined) {
939	      applyScrollTop(clampScrollTop(savedScrollTop, viewport.scrollHeight, viewport.clientHeight));

942	      scrollSettledRef.current = true;
943	    }
944	    // A mobile drawer whose selected row has not rendered yet stays unsettled so
945	    // that centring still runs once the run streams into the list.
946	  }, [getScrollViewport, mounted, runnerControlsMode, selectedRunId, sidebarContentKey]);

} from "./RunnerConnection";

type ProfileStoreLike = {
  getSnapshot(): RunnerProfileStoreSnapshot;
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
  setActiveRunner?(profileId: string): Promise<void>;
};

export type RunnerIdentityCollision = {
  runnerInstanceId: string;
  profileIds: string[];
};

export type RunnerRegistrySnapshot = {
  activeRunnerId: string | null;
  connections: RunnerConnectionSnapshot[];
  identityCollisions: RunnerIdentityCollision[];
};

export class RunnerRegistry extends StateManager<RunnerRegistrySnapshot> {
  private readonly profileStore: ProfileStoreLike;
  private readonly connectionFactory: (profile: RunnerProfile) => RunnerConnection;
  private readonly connections = new Map<string, RunnerConnection>();
  private readonly connectionUnsubscribes = new Map<string, () => void>();
  private profileUnsubscribe: (() => void) | null = null;
  private started = false;
  readonly previewCache = new BoundedRunnerPreviewCache<unknown>(300);

  constructor(options: {
    profileStore: ProfileStoreLike;
    connectionFactory: (profile: RunnerProfile) => RunnerConnection;
  }) {
    super({
      activeRunnerId: options.profileStore.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId ?? null,
      connections: [],
      identityCollisions: [],
    });
    this.profileStore = options.profileStore;
    this.connectionFactory = options.connectionFactory;
  }

  async start() {
    if (this.started) return;
    const profileSnapshot = this.profileStore.getSnapshot();
    this.reconcile(profileSnapshot.profiles);
    this.started = true;
    this.switchActive(profileSnapshot.activeRunnerId);
    this.profileUnsubscribe = this.profileStore.subscribe(() => {
      const next = this.profileStore.getSnapshot();
      this.reconcile(next.profiles);
      if (next.activeRunnerId !== this.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId) {
        this.switchActive(next.activeRunnerId, false);
      }
    });
    await Promise.all([...this.connections.values()].map((connection) => connection.start()));
  }

  stop() {
    this.started = false;
    this.profileUnsubscribe?.();
    this.profileUnsubscribe = null;
    for (const unsubscribe of this.connectionUnsubscribes.values()) {
      unsubscribe();
    }
    this.connectionUnsubscribes.clear();
    for (const connection of this.connections.values()) {
      connection.stop();
    }
    this.connections.clear();
    this.publish();
  }

  reconcile(profiles: RunnerProfile[]) {
    const nextIds = new Set(profiles.map((profile) => profile.id));
    for (const [profileId, connection] of this.connections) {
      if (nextIds.has(profileId)) continue;
      this.connectionUnsubscribes.get(profileId)?.();
      this.connectionUnsubscribes.delete(profileId);
      connection.stop();
      this.connections.delete(profileId);
    }
    for (const profile of profiles) {
      const existing = this.connections.get(profile.id);
      if (existing) {
        existing.updateProfile(profile);
        continue;
      }
      const connection = this.connectionFactory(profile);
      this.connections.set(profile.id, connection);
      this.connectionUnsubscribes.set(profile.id, connection.subscribe(() => {
        this.publish();
      }));
      if (this.started) {
        void connection.start();
      }
    }
    const activeRunnerId = this.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId;
    if (activeRunnerId && !this.connections.has(activeRunnerId)) {
      this.patch({
        activeRunnerId: profiles[0]?.id ?? null,
      }, false);
    }
    this.publish();
  }

  getConnection(profileId: string) {
    return this.connections.get(profileId) ?? null;
  }

  getActiveConnection() {
    const active = this.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId;
    return active ? this.getConnection(active) : null;
  }

  retryRecoverableConnections() {
    for (const connection of this.connections.values()) {
      const status = connection.getSnapshot().status;
      if (status === "offline") {
        void connection.retry();
      }
    }
  }

  switchActive(profileId: string, persist = true) {
    if (!this.connections.has(profileId)) {
      return false;
    }
    for (const [id, connection] of this.connections) {
      connection.setActive(id === profileId);
    }
    this.patch({ activeRunnerId: profileId }, false);
    this.publish();
    if (persist) {
      void this.profileStore.setActiveRunner?.(profileId);
    }
    return true;
  }

  resolveActiveRun(runId: string) {
    const runnerId = this.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId;
    const connection = runnerId ? this.connections.get(runnerId) : null;
    if (!runnerId || !connection) {
      return { status: "loading" as const, runnerId, runId };
    }
    const state = connection.getSnapshot();
    if (state.status === "connecting" || !state.snapshot) {
      return { status: "loading" as const, runnerId, runId };
    }
    const runs = Array.isArray(state.snapshot.runs)
      ? state.snapshot.runs as Array<{ id?: unknown }>
      : [];
    return runs.some((run) => run.id === runId)
      ? { status: "found" as const, runnerId, runId }
      : { status: "not_found" as const, runnerId, runId };
  }

  private publish() {
    const snapshots = [...this.connections.values()].map(
      (connection) => connection.getSnapshot(),
    );
    const byIdentity = new Map<string, string[]>();
    for (const snapshot of snapshots) {
      if (!snapshot.runnerInstanceId || snapshot.status !== "online") continue;
      const profiles = byIdentity.get(snapshot.runnerInstanceId) ?? [];
      profiles.push(snapshot.profileId);
      byIdentity.set(snapshot.runnerInstanceId, profiles);
    }
    const identityCollisions = [...byIdentity]
      .filter(([, profileIds]) => profileIds.length > 1)
      .map(([runnerInstanceId, profileIds]) => ({
        runnerInstanceId,
        profileIds: [...profileIds].sort(),
      }));
    this.update({
      activeRunnerId: this.getSnapshot().activeRunnerId,
      connections: snapshots,
      identityCollisions,
    });
  }
}

export function runnerStatusMessageKey(status: RunnerConnectionStatus) {
  return ({
    connecting: "runner.status.connecting",
    online: "runner.status.online",
    offline: "runner.status.offline",
    deferred: "runner.status.deferred",
    "needs-reauth": "runner.status.needsReauth",
    "tls-untrusted": "runner.status.tlsUntrusted",
    "identity-mismatch": "runner.status.identityMismatch",
    incompatible: "runner.status.incompatible",
    resync: "runner.status.resync",
    "runner-stopping": "runner.status.stopping",
  } satisfies Record<RunnerConnectionStatus, string>)[status];
}

export function countRunnerActivity(
  snapshot: RunnerConnectionSnapshot["snapshot"],
) {
  const runs = Array.isArray(snapshot?.runs)
    ? snapshot.runs as Array<{ status?: unknown }>
    : [];
  return runs.reduce((counts, run) => {
    const status = typeof run.status === "string"
      ? run.status.trim().toLowerCase()
      : "";
    if (status === "awaiting_user" || status === "needs_input") {
      counts.needsInput += 1;
    } else if (
      status === "running"
      || status === "planning"
      || status === "implementation"
    ) {
      counts.running += 1;
    }
    return counts;
  }, { needsInput: 0, running: 0 });
}

export class RunnerUiManager extends StateManager<RunnerUiSnapshot> {
  private readonly focusElement: (id: string) => void;

  constructor(options: {
    focusElement?: (id: string) => void;
  } = {}) {
    super(initialSnapshot);
    this.focusElement = options.focusElement ?? ((id) => {
      if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
        document.getElementById(id)?.focus();
      }
    });
  }

  openAdd(returnFocusId: string) {
    this.update({ ...initialSnapshot, dialog: "add", returnFocusId });
  }

  openEdit(
    profile: {
      id: string;
      label: string;
      baseUrl: string;
      savedPassword?: string | null;
    },
    returnFocusId: string,
  ) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog: "edit",
      profileId: profile.id,
      label: profile.label,
      baseUrl: profile.baseUrl,
      password: [REDACTED] ?? "",
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }

  openForget(profileId: string, returnFocusId: string) {
    this.openProfileDialog("forget", profileId, returnFocusId);
  }

  /**
   * Restart is offered for every server the client is connected to, not just
   * the one serving the page, so the confirmation has to name its target. The
   * name rides in `label` the way `openRename` uses it — a restart dialog that
   * only knew a profile id could not tell the reader which machine it was
   * about to stop.
   */
  openRestart(profileId: string, runnerName: string, returnFocusId: string) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog: "restart",
      profileId,
      label: runnerName,
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }

  openSessions(profileId: string, returnFocusId: string) {
    this.openProfileDialog("sessions", profileId, returnFocusId);
  }

  openRename(
    profileId: string,
    runnerName: string,
    returnFocusId: string,
  ) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog: "rename",
      profileId,
      label: runnerName,
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }

  openTlsConfirmation(
    profileId: string,
    fingerprint: string,
    returnFocusId: string,
  ) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog: "tls",
      profileId,
      fingerprint,
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }

  openIdentityMismatch(
    profileId: string,
    expectedIdentity: string,
    observedIdentity: string,
    returnFocusId: string,
  ) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog: "identity",
      profileId,
      expectedIdentity,
      observedIdentity,
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }

  setDraft(patch: { label?: string; baseUrl?: string; password?: string }) {
    this.patch(patch);
  }

  setBusy(busy: boolean) {
    this.patch({ busy, ...(busy ? { errorCode: null } : {}) });
  }

  setError(errorCode: string) {
    this.patch({ busy: false, errorCode });
  }

  setSessions(sessions: RunnerUiSnapshot["sessions"]) {
    this.patch({ sessions, busy: false, errorCode: null });
  }

  close() {
    const returnFocusId = this.getSnapshot().returnFocusId;
    this.update(initialSnapshot);
    if (returnFocusId) {
      queueMicrotask(() => this.focusElement(returnFocusId));
    }
  }

  private openProfileDialog(
    dialog: RunnerUiDialog,
    profileId: string,
    returnFocusId: string,
  ) {
    this.update({
      ...initialSnapshot,
      dialog,
      profileId,
      returnFocusId,
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Is this page served over HTTPS while the server speaks plain HTTP?
 *
 * The browser owns this decision, not the page and not the server: an HTTPS
 * document may not issue requests to an `http://` origin, and no header, flag
 * or fetch option opts back in. Only the page origin decides, so the native
 * surfaces stay exempt by passing their own `http://127.0.0.1` origin.
 */
export function isInsecureServerFromSecurePage(
  pageOrigin: string,
  baseUrl: string,
) {
  try {
    return new URL(pageOrigin).protocol === "https:"
      && new URL(baseUrl).protocol === "http:";
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Loopback addresses are potentially trustworthy origins, so browsers exempt
 * them from mixed-content blocking and `http://localhost` can still answer an
 * HTTPS page. Every other `http://` address is refused before the request is
 * ever sent, which is knowable up front rather than only after it fails.
 */
export function isMixedContentBlocked(pageOrigin: string, baseUrl: string) {
  if (!isInsecureServerFromSecurePage(pageOrigin, baseUrl)) {
    return false;
  }
  const host = new URL(baseUrl).hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^\[|\]$/g, "");
  const loopback = host === "localhost"
    || host.endsWith(".localhost")
    || host === "::1"
    || /^127(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}$/.test(host);
  return !loopback;
}

115	  const jittered = exponential * (0.5 + Math.max(0, Math.min(1, random)));
116	  return Math.min(300_000, Math.max(250, Math.round(jittered)));
117	}
118	
119	function normalizeRuntimeError(error: unknown): RuntimeApiError {
120	  if (error && typeof error === "object") {
121	    const candidate = error as Partial<RuntimeApiError> & { status?: unknown };
122	    const status = typeof candidate.status === "number" ? candidate.status : null;
123	    return {
124	      code: typeof candidate.code === "string"
125	        ? candidate.code
126	        : status
127	          ? `runtime.http_${status}`
128	          : "runtime.connection_failed",
129	      message: typeof candidate.message === "string"
130	        ? candidate.message
131	        : "Server connection failed.",
132	      ...(candidate.details !== undefined ? { details: candidate.details } : {}),
133	    };
134	  }
135	  return {
136	    code: "runtime.connection_failed",
137	    message: String(error),
138	  };
139	}
140	
141	function statusForError(error: RuntimeApiError): RunnerConnectionStatus {
142	  const code = error.code.toLowerCase();
143	  if (
144	    code.includes("401")
145	    || code.includes("unauthorized")
146	    || code.includes("auth")
147	    || code.includes("login")
148	  ) {
149	    return "needs-reauth";
150	  }
151	  if (code.includes("tls") || code.includes("certificate")) {
152	    return "tls-untrusted";
153	  }
154	  if (code.includes("deferred")) {
155	    return "deferred";
156	  }
157	  return "offline";
158	}
159	
160	function isBootstrapPayload(value: unknown): value is {
161	  runner: RunnerBootstrapIdentity;
162	  initialEventState?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
163	  initialLastEventId?: string | null;
164	  initialQueries?: {
165	    session?: {
166	      enabled?: boolean;
167	      authenticated?: boolean;
168	    } | null;
169	  };
170	} {
171	  if (!value || typeof value !== "object") {
172	    return false;
173	  }
174	  const runner = (value as { runner?: unknown }).runner;
175	  return Boolean(
176	    runner
177	    && typeof runner === "object"
178	    && typeof (runner as { runnerInstanceId?: unknown }).runnerInstanceId === "string"
179	    && typeof (runner as { name?: unknown }).name === "string",
180	  );
181	}
182	
183	export class BoundedRunnerPreviewCache<T> {
184	  private readonly entries = new Map<string, T>();
185	  constructor(private readonly maximumEntries = 100) {}
186	
187	  get(key: string) {
188	    const value = this.entries.get(key);
189	    if (value === undefined) return undefined;
190	    this.entries.delete(key);
191	    this.entries.set(key, value);
192	    return value;
193	  }
194	
195	  set(key: string, value: T) {
196	    this.entries.delete(key);
197	    this.entries.set(key, value);
198	    while (this.entries.size > this.maximumEntries) {
199	      const oldest = this.entries.keys().next().value;
200	      if (oldest === undefined) break;
201	      this.entries.delete(oldest);
202	    }
203	  }
204	
205	  clear() {
206	    this.entries.clear();
207	  }
208	
209	  get size() {
210	    return this.entries.size;
211	  }
212	}

214	export class RunnerConnection extends StateManager<RunnerConnectionSnapshot> {
215	  private profile: RunnerProfile;
216	  private readonly runtimeFactory: (profile: RunnerProfile) => Promise<RunnerConnectionRuntime>;
217	  private readonly persistence: RunnerConnectionPersistence;
218	  private readonly queryClient: QueryClient;
219	  private readonly now: () => number;
220	  private readonly schedule: (callback: () => void, delay: number) => ScheduleHandle;
221	  private readonly cancelSchedule: (handle: ScheduleHandle) => void;
222	  private readonly random: () => number;
223	  private readonly onIdentity?: (connection: RunnerConnection) => void;
224	  private runtime: RunnerConnectionRuntime | null = null;
225	  private mainStream: RuntimeSubscription | null = null;
226	  private readonly terminalStreams = new Map<string, RuntimeSubscription>();
227	  private retryTimer: ScheduleHandle | null = null;
228	  private retryAttempt = 0;
229	  private reconnectGraceTimer: ScheduleHandle | null = null;
230	  /**
231	   * Set by any stream drop, cleared when the stream reopens. Tracked apart from
232	   * the visible status because the grace period deliberately keeps a brief drop
233	   * out of the UI, while requests issued during that drop still failed and
234	   * still need retrying once the stream is back.
235	   */
236	  private streamInterrupted = false;
237	  private readonly streamReconnectGraceMs: number;
238	  private generation = 0;
239	  private started = false;
240	  private connecting: Promise<void> | null = null;
241	  private resyncing = false;
242	  private cursor: string | null;
243	  private readonly resyncTimes: number[] = [];
244	  readonly previewCache = new BoundedRunnerPreviewCache<unknown>();
245	
246	  constructor(options: {
247	    profile: RunnerProfile;
248	    runtimeFactory: (profile: RunnerProfile) => Promise<RunnerConnectionRuntime>;
249	    persistence: RunnerConnectionPersistence;
250	    queryClient?: QueryClient;
251	    now?: () => number;
252	    schedule?: (callback: () => void, delay: number) => ScheduleHandle;
253	    cancelSchedule?: (handle: ScheduleHandle) => void;
254	    random?: () => number;
255	    streamReconnectGraceMs?: number;
256	    onIdentity?: (connection: RunnerConnection) => void;
257	  }) {
258	    super({
259	      profileId: options.profile.id,
260	      status: "offline",
261	      active: false,
262	      runnerInstanceId: options.profile.runnerInstanceId,
263	      runnerName: options.profile.label,
264	      observedRunnerInstanceId: null,
265	      lastError: null,
266	      retryAt: null,
267	      resyncCount: 0,
268	      snapshot: null,
269	      bootstrap: null,
270	    });
271	    this.profile = options.profile;
272	    this.runtimeFactory = options.runtimeFactory;
273	    this.persistence = options.persistence;
274	    this.queryClient = options.queryClient ?? new QueryClient();
275	    this.now = options.now ?? Date.now;
276	    this.schedule = options.schedule ?? ((callback, delay) => setTimeout(callback, delay));
277	    this.cancelSchedule = options.cancelSchedule ?? ((handle) => {
278	      clearTimeout(handle as ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>);
279	    });
280	    this.random = options.random ?? Math.random;
281	    this.streamReconnectGraceMs = options.streamReconnectGraceMs ?? STREAM_RECONNECT_GRACE_MS;
282	    this.onIdentity = options.onIdentity;
283	    this.cursor = options.persistence.getScopedState(options.profile.id).cursors.events || null;
284	  }
285	
286	  getQueryClient() {
287	    return this.queryClient;
288	  }
289	
290	  getRuntimeAPIs() {
291	    return this.runtime?.apis ?? null;
292	  }
293	
294	  async authenticateWithPassword(input: { password: string; label: string }) {
295	    this.profile = this.persistence.getProfile(this.profile.id) ?? this.profile;
296	    const profile = this.profile;
297	    const generation = ++this.generation;
298	    this.clearRetry();
299	    const runtime = this.runtime ?? await this.runtimeFactory(profile);
300	    if (
301	      generation !== this.generation
302	      || (this.persistence.getProfile(profile.id) ?? profile).baseUrl !== profile.baseUrl
303	      || !runtime.apis
304	    ) {
305	      throw { code: "runner.error.generic" };
306	    }
307	    await runtime.apis.auth.login(input);
308	    if (
309	      generation !== this.generation
310	      || (this.persistence.getProfile(profile.id) ?? profile).baseUrl !== profile.baseUrl
311	    ) {
312	      throw { code: "runner.error.generic" };
313	    }
314	    await this.retry();
315	  }
316	
317	  updateProfile(nextProfile: RunnerProfile) {
318	    const authenticationChanged = (
319	      nextProfile.baseUrl !== this.profile.baseUrl
320	      || nextProfile.credentialRef !== this.profile.credentialRef
321	      || nextProfile.authTransport !== this.profile.authTransport
322	    );
323	    this.profile = nextProfile;
324	    if (!authenticationChanged || !this.started) {
325	      return;
326	    }
327	    this.generation += 1;
328	    this.mainStream?.close();
329	    this.mainStream = null;
330	    this.closeTerminalStreams();
331	    this.runtime = null;
332	    void this.connect();
333	  }
334	
335	  queryKey(...parts: readonly unknown[]) {
336	    return [this.getSnapshot().runnerInstanceId ?? this.profile.id, ...parts] as const;
337	  }
338	
339	  async start() {
340	    if (this.started) {
341	      return this.connecting ?? Promise.resolve();
342	    }
343	    this.started = true;
344	    return this.connect();
345	  }
346	
347	  retry() {
348	    if (!this.started) {
349	      return this.start();
350	    }
351	    return this.connect();
352	  }
353	
354	  private async connect() {
355	    const generation = ++this.generation;
356	    this.clearRetry();
357	    this.patch({
358	      status: "connecting",
359	      retryAt: null,
360	      lastError: null,
361	    });
362	    const operation = this.connectGeneration(generation);
363	    this.connecting = operation;
364	    try {
365	      await operation;
366	    } finally {
367	      if (this.connecting === operation) {
368	        this.connecting = null;
369	      }
370	    }
371	  }
372	
373	  private async connectGeneration(generation: number) {
374	    try {
375	      this.profile = this.persistence.getProfile(this.profile.id) ?? this.profile;
376	      const runtime = await this.runtimeFactory(this.profile);
377	      const loadCompatibleBootstrap = async () => {
378	        const candidate = await runtime.bootstrap.load({});
379	        if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return null;
380	        if (!isBootstrapPayload(candidate)) {
381	          throw {
382	            code: "runtime.bootstrap_invalid",
383	            message: "Server bootstrap response is invalid.",
384	          };
385	        }
386	        const compatibility = assessApiCompatibility(candidate.runner);
387	        if (!compatibility.compatible) {
388	          this.patch({
389	            status: "incompatible",
390	            observedRunnerInstanceId: candidate.runner.runnerInstanceId,
391	            lastError: {
392	              code: "runtime.incompatible",
393	              message: "Server API revisions are incompatible.",
394	            },
395	          });
396	          return null;
397	        }
398	        return candidate;
399	      };
400	
401	      let payload = await loadCompatibleBootstrap();
402	      if (!payload) return;
403	      const session = payload.initialQueries?.session;
404	      if (
405	        this.profile.isSameOrigin
406	        && this.profile.savedPassword
407	        && session?.enabled
408	        && !session.authenticated
409	        && runtime.apis
410	      ) {
411	        await runtime.apis.auth.login({
412	          password: [REDACTED]
413	          label: "Browser session",
414	        });
415	        if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
416	        payload = await loadCompatibleBootstrap();
417	        if (!payload) return;
418	      }
419	      const identity = await this.persistence.learnIdentity(
420	        this.profile.id,
421	        payload.runner.runnerInstanceId,
422	        {
423	          validSameOriginSession: this.profile.isSameOrigin,
424	        },
425	      );
426	      if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
427	      if (identity.status === "identity_mismatch") {
428	        this.patch({
429	          status: "identity-mismatch",
430	          observedRunnerInstanceId: identity.observedRunnerInstanceId,
431	          lastError: {
432	            code: "runner.identity_mismatch",
433	            message: "The endpoint reports a different server identity.",
434	          },
435	        });
436	        return;
437	      }
438	      this.profile = this.persistence.getProfile(identity.profileId) ?? {
439	        ...this.profile,
440	        runnerInstanceId: payload.runner.runnerInstanceId,
441	      };
442	      this.runtime = runtime;
443	      this.retryAttempt = 0;
444	      if (payload.initialLastEventId) {
445	        await this.persistCursor(payload.initialLastEventId);
446	      }
447	      this.patch({
448	        status: payload.runner.readinessState === "stopping"
449	          ? "runner-stopping"
450	          : "online",
451	        runnerInstanceId: payload.runner.runnerInstanceId,
452	        runnerName: payload.runner.name,
453	        observedRunnerInstanceId: null,
454	        snapshot: payload.initialEventState ?? null,
455	        bootstrap: payload as HomeBootstrapPayload,
456	        lastError: null,
457	        retryAt: null,
458	      });
459	      this.onIdentity?.(this);
460	      const authenticatedSession = payload.initialQueries?.session;
461	      if (authenticatedSession?.enabled && !authenticatedSession.authenticated) {
462	        this.patch({
463	          status: "needs-reauth",
464	          lastError: {
465	            code: "runtime.http_401",
466	            message: "Server authorization is required.",
467	          },
468	        });
469	      } else if (payload.runner.readinessState !== "stopping") {
470	        this.openMainStream(generation);
471	      }
472	    } catch (error) {
473	      if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
474	      this.handleConnectionError(normalizeRuntimeError(error));
475	    }
476	  }
477	
478	  private isCurrent(generation: number) {
479	    return this.started && generation === this.generation;
480	  }
481	
482	  private openMainStream(generation: number) {
483	    if (!this.runtime || !this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
484	    this.mainStream?.close();
485	    this.mainStream = this.runtime.events.open({
486	      snapshot: false,
487	      runId: null,
488	      lastEventId: this.cursor,
489	    }, {
490	      onOpen: () => {
491	        if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
492	        this.retryAttempt = 0;
493	        this.clearRetry();
494	        this.clearReconnectGraceTimer();
495	        const wasInterrupted = this.streamInterrupted
496	          || this.getSnapshot().status !== "online";
497	        this.streamInterrupted = false;
498	        if (this.getSnapshot().status !== "runner-stopping") {
499	          this.patch({ status: "online", retryAt: null, lastError: null });
500	        }
501	        // Requests that failed while this runner was unreachable keep their
502	        // error until something fetches them again, and nothing else does.
503	        // Keyed on the interruption rather than the visible status, so a drop
504	        // short enough to stay inside the grace period still clears them.
505	        if (wasInterrupted) {
506	          void refetchFailedQueries(this.queryClient);
507	        }
508	      },
509	      onEvent: (event) => {
510	        if (this.isCurrent(generation)) {
511	          void this.handleStreamEvent(event, generation);
512	        }
513	      },
514	      onError: (error) => {
515	        if (this.isCurrent(generation)) {
516	          if (error.code === "runtime.events_reconnecting") {
517	            if (this.getSnapshot().status !== "runner-stopping") {
518	              this.noteStreamInterrupted(error, generation);
519	            }
520	            return;
521	          }
522	          this.handleConnectionError(error);
523	        }
524	      },
525	    });
526	  }
527	
528	  private async handleStreamEvent(event: unknown, generation: number) {
529	    if (!event || typeof event !== "object") return;
530	    const frame = event as {
531	      kind?: string;
532	      payload?: unknown;
533	      lastEventId?: string | null;
534	    };
535	    if (frame.kind === "stream.resync_required") {
536	      await this.handleResync(generation);
537	      return;
538	    }
539	    if (frame.kind === "runner.stopping") {
540	      this.patch({ status: "runner-stopping" });
541	      return;
542	    }
543	    if (frame.kind === "auth.session_revoked") {
544	      this.patch({
545	        status: "needs-reauth",
546	        lastError: {
547	          code: "runtime.http_401",
548	          message: "Server authorization is required.",
549	        },
550	        retryAt: null,
551	      });
552	      this.mainStream?.close();
553	      this.mainStream = null;
554	      this.closeTerminalStreams();
555	      return;
556	    }
557	    if (frame.kind === "runner.renamed") {
558	      const name = (frame as { name?: unknown }).name;
559	      if (typeof name === "string" && name.trim()) {
560	        this.patch({ runnerName: name.trim() });
561	      }
562	      return;
563	    }
564	    if (frame.kind === "runner.rekeyed") {
565	      const observed = (frame as { runnerInstanceId?: unknown }).runnerInstanceId;
566	      if (
567	        typeof observed === "string"
568	        && observed
569	        && observed !== this.getSnapshot().runnerInstanceId
570	      ) {
571	        this.patch({
572	          status: "identity-mismatch",
573	          observedRunnerInstanceId: observed,
574	          lastError: {
575	            code: "runner.identity_mismatch",
576	            message: "The server was rekeyed and needs identity confirmation.",
577	          },
578	        });
579	      }
580	      return;
581	    }
582	    if (frame.lastEventId) {
583	      await this.persistCursor(frame.lastEventId);
584	    }
585	    if (frame.kind === "update" && frame.payload && typeof frame.payload === "object") {
586	      this.patch({ snapshot: frame.payload as Record<string, unknown> });
587	    }
588	  }
589	
590	  private async persistCursor(cursor: string) {
591	    this.cursor = cursor || null;
592	    await this.persistence.updateScopedState(this.profile.id, {
593	      cursors: { events: cursor },
594	    });
595	  }
596	
597	  private async handleResync(generation: number) {
598	    if (!this.runtime || !this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
599	    const now = this.now();
600	    this.resyncTimes.push(now);
601	    while (this.resyncTimes[0] !== undefined && now - this.resyncTimes[0] > 5 * 60_000) {
602	      this.resyncTimes.shift();
603	    }
604	    this.patch({ resyncCount: this.resyncTimes.length });
605	    if (this.resyncTimes.length > 3) {
606	      this.mainStream?.close();
607	      this.mainStream = null;
608	      await this.persistCursor("");
609	      // Backing off is a reconnect like any other; the user sees "Connecting"
610	      // until it lands, not a verdict on the connection's quality.
611	      this.patch({
612	        status: "connecting",
613	        lastError: {
614	          code: "runtime.resync_storm",
615	          message: "Repeated stream resynchronization entered backoff.",
616	        },
617	      });
618	      this.scheduleReconnect();
619	      return;
620	    }
621	    if (this.resyncing) return;
622	    this.resyncing = true;
623	    await this.persistCursor("");
624	    this.mainStream?.close();
625	    this.mainStream = null;
626	    this.patch({ status: "resync" });
627	    try {
628	      const result = await this.runtime.events.snapshot({ persisted: true });
629	      if (!this.isCurrent(generation)) return;
630	      // A resync storm closed the stream and scheduled a fresh connection
631	      // while this snapshot was in flight; that connection owns the stream now.
632	      if (this.retryTimer) return;
633	      if (result.lastEventId) {
634	        await this.persistCursor(result.lastEventId);
635	      }
636	      if (result.data && typeof result.data === "object") {
637	        this.patch({ snapshot: result.data as Record<string, unknown> });
638	      }
639	      this.openMainStream(generation);
640	      this.patch({ status: "online" });
641	    } catch (error) {
642	      if (this.isCurrent(generation)) {
643	        this.handleConnectionError(normalizeRuntimeError(error));
644	      }
645	    } finally {
646	      this.resyncing = false;
647	    }
648	  }
649	
650	  /**
651	   * Record a stream drop the browser is already retrying. The runner stays
652	   * "online" for the grace period; only if the stream has not come back by
653	   * then does the connection show "connecting" and take over the reconnect
654	   * itself. There is no intermediate state: a blip the browser heals is
655	   * invisible, and one it cannot heal becomes an ordinary reconnect.
656	   */
657	  private noteStreamInterrupted(error: RuntimeApiError, generation: number) {
658	    this.streamInterrupted = true;
659	    if (this.reconnectGraceTimer) return;
660	    this.reconnectGraceTimer = this.schedule(() => {
661	      this.reconnectGraceTimer = null;
662	      if (!this.isCurrent(generation) || !this.streamInterrupted) return;
663	      if (this.getSnapshot().status === "runner-stopping") return;
664	      this.patch({ status: "connecting", lastError: error, retryAt: null });
665	      this.scheduleReconnect();
666	    }, this.streamReconnectGraceMs);
667	  }
668	
669	  private clearReconnectGraceTimer() {
670	    if (!this.reconnectGraceTimer) return;
671	    this.cancelSchedule(this.reconnectGraceTimer);
672	    this.reconnectGraceTimer = null;
673	  }
674	
675	  private handleConnectionError(error: RuntimeApiError) {
676	    const status = statusForError(error);
677	    this.clearReconnectGraceTimer();
678	    this.streamInterrupted = true;
679	    this.patch({ status, lastError: error });
680	    this.mainStream?.close();
681	    this.mainStream = null;
682	    if (status === "offline") {
683	      this.scheduleReconnect();
684	    }
685	  }
686	
687	  private scheduleReconnect() {
688	    if (!this.started || this.retryTimer) return;
689	    const delay = calculateRunnerReconnectDelay(this.retryAttempt, this.random());
690	    this.retryAttempt += 1;
691	    this.patch({ retryAt: this.now() + delay });
692	    this.retryTimer = this.schedule(() => {
693	      this.retryTimer = null;
694	      if (this.started) {
695	        void this.connect();
696	      }
697	    }, delay);
698	  }
699	
700	  private clearRetry() {
701	    if (!this.retryTimer) return;
702	    this.cancelSchedule(this.retryTimer);
703	    this.retryTimer = null;
704	  }
705	
706	  stop() {
707	    this.started = false;
708	    this.generation += 1;
709	    this.clearRetry();
710	    this.clearReconnectGraceTimer();
711	    this.streamInterrupted = false;
712	    this.mainStream?.close();
713	    this.mainStream = null;
714	    this.closeTerminalStreams();
715	    this.runtime = null;
716	    this.patch({
717	      status: "offline",
718	      retryAt: null,
719	    });
720	  }
721	
722	  setActive(active: boolean) {
723	    this.patch({ active });
724	    if (!active) {
725	      this.closeTerminalStreams();
726	    }
727	  }
728	
729	  openTerminalStream(
730	    terminalId: string,
731	    handlers: RunnerStreamHandlers,
732	    lastEventId?: string | null,
733	  ) {
734	    if (!this.getSnapshot().active || !this.runtime) {
735	      throw new Error("Terminal streams are available only on the active server.");
736	    }
737	    this.terminalStreams.get(terminalId)?.close();
738	    const subscription = this.runtime.terminals.openStream(
739	      { terminalId, lastEventId },
740	      handlers,
741	    );
742	    this.terminalStreams.set(terminalId, subscription);
743	    return {
744	      close: () => {
745	        if (this.terminalStreams.get(terminalId) === subscription) {
746	          this.terminalStreams.delete(terminalId);
747	        }
748	        subscription.close();
749	      },
750	    };
751	  }
752	
753	  private closeTerminalStreams() {
754	    for (const subscription of this.terminalStreams.values()) {
755	      subscription.close();
756	    }
757	    this.terminalStreams.clear();
758	  }
759	}

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:04:49.210Z

Each runner connection keeps a live event snapshot including runs and possibly projects, so I should check what that snapshot contains and how the sidebar groups projects via filteredProjects in useHomeViewModel. I also need to figure out where projects are persisted server-side and how reordering works, since the key design question is what happens when a user clicks a project.

If a pinned project lives on a non-active runner, clicking it should switch the active runner then select the run, since the app is active-runner-centric — I need to check resolveActiveRun and RunnerRegistryProvider for how that switch-then-navigate flow works. For persistence, storing pins client-side per browser is simplest for aggregating across servers, but storing a pinned flag on each project server-side is more robust since it syncs across devices and doesn't depend on which client is viewing it — though this depends on whether the event snapshot for non-active runners actually includes project data, which I need to verify.

268	          || observedSnapshots.get(connection.profileId) === connection.snapshot
269	        ) {
270	          continue;
271	        }
272	        observedSnapshots.set(connection.profileId, connection.snapshot);
273	        conversationNotificationManager.handleRunnerEventStreamState({
274	          profileId: connection.profileId,
275	          runnerInstanceId: connection.runnerInstanceId,
276	          runnerName: connection.runnerName,
277	          listEntries: registry.getConnection(connection.profileId)?.getRuntimeAPIs()?.workers.listEntries,
278	        }, connection.snapshot as unknown as EventStreamState);
279	      }
280	    };
281	    observe();
282	    return registry.subscribe(observe);
283	  }, [registry]);

286	    registry,
287	    windowTarget: window,
288	    documentTarget: document,
289	    isVisible: () => document.visibilityState === "visible",
290	  }), [registry]);
291	
292	  return (
293	    <RunnerRegistryContext.Provider value={{
294	      registry,

296	      credentialStore,
297	      uiManager,
298	    }}>
299	      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>

307	  const value = useContext(RunnerRegistryContext);

310	  }
311	  return value.registry;
312	}
313

316	}

318	export function useRunnerRegistryContext() {
319	  const value = useOptionalRunnerRegistryContext();
320	  if (!value) {

322	  }
323	  return value;
324	}

326	export function useRunnerConnections() {
327	  const registry = useRunnerRegistry();
328	  return useRegistrySnapshot(registry).connections;
