1	"use client";
2	
3	import { lazy, Suspense, useMemo } from "react";
4	import { BootShell } from "@/components/BootShell";
5	import type { RunnerConnectionStatus } from "@/interface/runners/RunnerConnection";
6	import { RunnerControls } from "@/interface/runners/RunnerControls";
7	import { runnerStatusMessageKey } from "@/interface/runners/RunnerUiManager";
8	import type { HomeBootstrapPayload } from "@/shared/bootstrap";
9	import type { RuntimeAPIs } from "@/runtime-api/types";
10	import { t, useI18nSnapshot } from "@/lib/i18n";
11	import { RuntimeApiProvider, createDefaultWebRuntimeAPIs } from "@/runtime-api/provider";
12	import {
13	  RunnerRegistryProvider,
14	  createDefaultRunnerRegistry,
15	  useActiveRunnerConnection,
16	  useRunnerConnections,
17	} from "@/interface/runners/RunnerRegistryProvider";
18	
19	const HomeApp = lazy(
20	  () => import("@/interface/home/HomeApp").then((module) => ({ default: module.HomeApp })),
21	);
22	
23	export function OmniApp({
24	  bootstrap,
25	  runtimeApis,
26	}: {
27	  bootstrap: HomeBootstrapPayload;
28	  runtimeApis?: RuntimeAPIs;
29	}) {
30	  const defaultRuntimeApis = useMemo(() => runtimeApis ?? createDefaultWebRuntimeAPIs(), [runtimeApis]);
31	  const runnerSetup = useMemo(() => createDefaultRunnerRegistry(), []);
32	
33	  if (defaultRuntimeApis.runtime.surface === "vscode") {
34	    return (
35	      <RuntimeApiProvider apis={defaultRuntimeApis}>
36	        <Suspense fallback={<BootShell />}>
37	          <HomeApp bootstrap={bootstrap} />
38	        </Suspense>
39	      </RuntimeApiProvider>
40	    );
41	  }
42	
43	  return (
44	    <RunnerRegistryProvider
45	      registry={runnerSetup.registry}
46	      profileStore={runnerSetup.profiles}
47	      credentialStore={runnerSetup.credentials}
48	      uiManager={runnerSetup.uiManager}
49	    >
50	      <ActiveRunnerApp />
51	    </RunnerRegistryProvider>
52	  );
53	}
54	
55	function ActiveRunnerApp() {
56	  useRunnerConnections();
57	  const connection = useActiveRunnerConnection();
58	  const connectionSnapshot = connection?.getSnapshot();
59	  const runtimeApis = connection?.getRuntimeAPIs();
60	  const bootstrap = connectionSnapshot?.bootstrap;
61	
62	  if (!connection) {
63	    return <BootShell />;
64	  }
65	
66	  if (!runtimeApis || !bootstrap) {
67	    return <RunnerRecoveryShell status={connectionSnapshot?.status ?? "connecting"} />;
68	  }
69	
70	  return (
71	    <RuntimeApiProvider apis={runtimeApis}>
72	      <Suspense fallback={<BootShell />}>
73	        <HomeApp
74	          key={connectionSnapshot.profileId}
75	          bootstrap={bootstrap}
76	          runnerConnection={connection}
77	        />
78	      </Suspense>
79	    </RuntimeApiProvider>
80	  );
81	}
82	
83	function RunnerRecoveryShell({
84	  status,
85	}: {
86	  status: RunnerConnectionStatus;
87	}) {
88	  useI18nSnapshot();
89	  return (
90	    <main className="relative flex h-dvh w-full flex-col overflow-hidden bg-background text-foreground">
91	      <header className="flex h-14 shrink-0 items-center gap-3 border-b border-border/60 px-3 sm:px-4">
92	        <span className="text-sm font-semibold">{t("product.name")}</span>
93	        <RunnerControls />
94	      </header>
95	      <section className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 items-center justify-center p-6">
96	        <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
97	          {t(runnerStatusMessageKey(status))}
98	        </p>
99	      </section>
100	    </main>
101	  );
102	}
103

import { type AppErrorDescriptor, normalizeAppError } from "@/lib/app-errors";
import type { ChatAttachment } from "@/lib/chat-attachments";
import { formatHumanDuration, type ConversationWorkerRecord } from "@/lib/conversation-workers";
import { isTerminalRunStatus } from "@/lib/run-status";
import { getLatestUnresolvedWorkerStuckEvent } from "@/lib/worker-stuck-events";
import { normalizeReasoningEffort } from "@/shared/reasoning-effort";
import { DEFAULT_COMPOSER_EFFORT, EFFORT_OPTIONS, RUN_PATH_PATTERN, WORKER_OPTIONS, FALLBACK_WORKER_MODEL_OPTIONS } from "./constants";
import type { AgentSnapshot, ConversationModeOption, EventStreamState, ExecutionEventRecord, MessageRecord, PlanItemRecord, PlanRecord, QueuedConversationMessageRecord, RunRecord, SupervisorInterventionRecord, WorkerModelCatalog, WorkerType } from "./types";
import { t } from "@/lib/i18n";

export { getLatestUnresolvedWorkerStuckEvent };

export type BrowserConversationRoute = {
  selectedRunId: string | null;
  draftProjectPath: string | null;
  pairTokenFromUrl: string | null;
};

export function parseBrowserConversationRoute(location: Pick<Location, "pathname" | "search">): BrowserConversationRoute {
  const pathnameMatch = location.pathname.match(RUN_PATH_PATTERN);
  const routeRunId = pathnameMatch?.[1]?.trim() || "";
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  const queryRunId = params.get("run")?.trim() || "";
  const selectedRunId = routeRunId || queryRunId || null;

  return {
    selectedRunId,
    draftProjectPath: selectedRunId ? null : params.get("project")?.trim() || null,
    pairTokenFromUrl: params.get("pair")?.trim() || null,
  };
}

export function buildInlineError(
  error: unknown,
  fallback: Partial<AppErrorDescriptor> = {},
): AppErrorDescriptor {
  return normalizeAppError(error, fallback);
}

export function shouldClearMissingSelectedRunFromAuthoritativeSnapshot(args: {
  selectedRunId: string | null | undefined;
  selectedRunExists: boolean;
  snapshotSource: EventStreamState["snapshotSource"];
  catalogComplete: boolean | undefined;
  snapshotRunId: string | null | undefined;
}) {
  return Boolean(
    args.selectedRunId
    && !args.selectedRunExists
    && args.snapshotSource === "server"
    && (
      args.catalogComplete === true
      || (
        args.catalogComplete === false
        && args.snapshotRunId === args.selectedRunId
      )
    ),
  );
}

export function resolveComposerEffortLabel(preferredEffort: string | null | undefined) {
  if (!preferredEffort?.trim()) {
    return null;
  }

  const normalized = preferredEffort.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (normalized === "low") {
    return "Low";
  }
  if (normalized === "medium") {
    return "Medium";
  }
  if (normalized === "high") {
    return "High";
  }
  if (normalized === "xhigh" || normalized === "extra high" || normalized === "extra-high") {
    return "Extra High";
  }
  if (normalized === "max") {
    return "Max";
  }

  return null;
}

export function buildConversationPath(selectedRunId: string | null, draftProjectPath: string | null) {
  if (selectedRunId) {
    return `/session/${selectedRunId}`;
  }

  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  if (draftProjectPath) {
    params.set("project", draftProjectPath);
  }

  const query = params.toString();
  return query ? `/?${query}` : "/";
}

export function createClientRunId() {
  if (typeof crypto !== "undefined" && typeof crypto.getRandomValues === "function") {
  }, [
    appUnlocked,
    authConfigurationError,
    authEnabled,
    pairRedeemAttempted,
    pairTokenFromUrl,
    redeemPairMutation,
    routeReady,
    setPairRedeemAttempted,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window === "undefined" || !routeReady) {
      return;
    }

    if (pairTokenFromUrl && !appUnlocked) {
      return;
    }

    const nextPath = buildConversationPath(selectedRunId, draftProjectPath);
    const currentPath = `${window.location.pathname}${window.location.search}`;
    if (currentPath !== nextPath) {
      window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", nextPath);
    }
  }, [appUnlocked, draftProjectPath, pairTokenFromUrl, routeReady, selectedRunId]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window === "undefined") {
      return;
    }

    try {
      setCollapsedProjectPaths(parseCollapsedProjectPaths(window.localStorage.getItem("omni-collapsed-projects")));
    } catch {
      setRuntimeErrors((current) => mergeAppErrors(current, [{
        message: "The saved project group state in localStorage is malformed.",
        source: "Frontend",
        action: "Restore local navigation state",
        suggestion: "Clear the omni-collapsed-projects localStorage entry and reload the page if project expansion looks wrong.",
      }]));

1	import type { HomeBootstrapPayload } from "@/shared/bootstrap";

4	import { homeUiStateManager } from "./HomeUiStateManager";
5	import { planningReviewPreferencesManager } from "./PlanningReviewPreferencesManager";
6	import { settingsDraftManager } from "./SettingsDraftManager";
7	import { parseBrowserConversationRoute } from "./utils";
8	
9	let appliedHomeBootstrapId: string | null = null;
10	let appliedRunnerInstanceId: string | null = null;
11	
12	export function applyHomeBootstrap(
13	  bootstrap: HomeBootstrapPayload | null | undefined,
14	  notify = true,
15	) {
16	  if (!bootstrap || appliedHomeBootstrapId === bootstrap.id) {
17	    return;
18	  }
19	
20	  appliedHomeBootstrapId = bootstrap.id;
21	  const browserRoute = typeof window === "undefined"
22	    ? bootstrap.route
23	    : parseBrowserConversationRoute(window.location);
24	  const routeSelectedRunId = browserRoute.selectedRunId;
25	  const settingsValues = bootstrap.initialQueries.settings?.values ?? {};
26	
27	  // Settings are per server, and a server only reports the keys it actually
28	  // stores. Merging a new server's settings over the previous server's leaves
29	  // every key the new one never saved — the project list above all — reading as
30	  // if it belonged to the server now on screen. Arriving from a different
31	  // server is therefore a replacement, not an update. A reconnect to the same
32	  // server stays a merge, so a bootstrap that arrives without settings (an
33	  // unauthenticated or degraded reply) cannot blank out live state.
34	  const runnerChanged = appliedRunnerInstanceId !== null
35	    && appliedRunnerInstanceId !== bootstrap.runner.runnerInstanceId;
36	  appliedRunnerInstanceId = bootstrap.runner.runnerInstanceId;
37	
38	  if (bootstrap.initialQueries.settings || runnerChanged) {
39	    settingsDraftManager.hydrate(settingsValues, notify, runnerChanged ? "replace" : "refresh");
40	    planningReviewPreferencesManager.hydrate(settingsValues);
41	  }
42	
43	  homeUiStateManager.patch((current) => ({
44	    routeReady: true,
45	    hasReceivedInitialEventStreamPayload: Boolean(bootstrap.initialEventState),
46	    selectedRunId: routeSelectedRunId,
47	    draftProjectPath: routeSelectedRunId ? null : browserRoute.draftProjectPath,
48	    pairTokenFromUrl: browserRoute.pairTokenFromUrl,
49	    apiKeys: runnerChanged
50	      ? { ...DEFAULT_SERVER_SETTINGS, ...settingsValues }
51	      : { ...current.apiKeys, ...settingsValues },
52	    settingsDiagnostics: runnerChanged
53	      ? bootstrap.initialQueries.settings?.diagnostics ?? []
54	      : bootstrap.initialQueries.settings?.diagnostics ?? current.settingsDiagnostics,
55	  }), notify);
56	
57	  const initialSnapshotRunId = bootstrap.initialEventState?.snapshotRunId?.trim();
58	  if (bootstrap.initialEventState?.queuedMessages && initialSnapshotRunId) {
59	    busyMessageQueueManager.setQueuedMessages(bootstrap.initialEventState.queuedMessages, {
60	      runId: initialSnapshotRunId,
61	      notify,
62	    });

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:05:46.083Z

When switching runners, HomeApp remounts and reapplies the bootstrap for whichever connection is active, so toggling A→B→A just reapplies A's bootstrap again since the last-applied id was B's. The selected run id is tracked via the URL, so cross-runner selection should update it with a replaceState call to the session path for that run.

I'm also checking how stale run selection from a previous runner gets handled — since existing logic clears a selected run that doesn't exist on the new runner, replacing the URL before switching should stay consistent. This mirrors the notification-click flow which uses the `?runner=` param, though that likely triggers a full page reload rather than an in-app switch.

Now for pinned projects: each connected runner needs its own project list and runs, which come through the connection's event snapshot updated via patch frames — though I need to confirm whether the global stream sends a full runs catalog or just a partial one. For storing pins, one option is a server-side per-server `PINNED_PROJECTS` setting read from each connection's bootstrap settings, but updating a pin for a non-active runner would require calling that connection's settings-save API, which saves the whole settings blob and risks staleness across devices.

Alternatively, I could store pins client-side in the RunnerProfileStore via localStorage (which works across Electron and Capacitor), either using the existing per-runner `preferences` field or a dedicated PinnedProjectsManager keyed by profileId and path — simpler and naturally client-scoped, though not synced across devices.

Still, there's a question of whether pins should instead live server-side for multi-device access, which is tricky since aggregating "pinned across servers" is inherently a client-side concept and profileIds can vary per device. I'm leaning toward keying by the stable runnerInstanceId instead of profileId, mapping it to the current profile via connections, before deciding whether settings.save can support this.

Actually, RunnerProfileStore already handles persistent per-runner client state with proper storage adapters, and Electron's storage might be file-backed rather than localStorage given the renderer origin differences. Let me look at how RunnerProfileStore handles scopedState preferences and its storage mechanism.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:05:59.570Z

I'm thinking that storing `preferences.pinnedProjects` as an array of path/pinnedAt pairs fits naturally into this per-runner scoped state, since forgetting a server drops its pins while identity merges preserve them with a simple shallow merge. For ordering, I'm considering sorting the pinned section by pinnedAt, earliest first.

I'm also noting that RunnerRegistry subscribes to profileStore and reconciles on every change, so persisting pins just triggers another harmless reconcile pass, similar to how cursors already persist constantly. For populating pinned groups, I'd pull from `connection.snapshot` for non-active runners filtered by project path, and from the live filteredProjects groups for the active runner — and like pinned chats in ChatGPT/Codex, pinned projects should move into the Pinned section and be removed from the normal list below to avoid duplicates.

I'm deciding the Pinned section should only appear in the Projects tab, not the Active tab, since the Active tab is already filtered to live conversations and showing pinned there would be confusing. I also need search to apply consistently — I'll check how filteredProjects builds grouping in useHomeViewModel so I can reuse that same logic for grouping remote snapshot runs under search.

function timestampMs(value: string | null | undefined) {
  if (!value) return 0;
  const parsed = new Date(value).getTime();
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;
}

/**
 * Order sessions by conversation activity, newest first.

 * `lastActivityAt` is written server-side on the last user message and the last

 * `ORDER BY` matters because `EventStreamStateManager` merges runs by id and
 * appends unseen ones to the end — an optimistically created run would
 * otherwise sink to the bottom of its project until the next full snapshot.

function compareConversationRunsDesc(
  a: { lastActivityAt?: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
  b: { lastActivityAt?: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
) {
  const activityDiff =
    Math.max(timestampMs(b.lastActivityAt), timestampMs(b.createdAt))
    - Math.max(timestampMs(a.lastActivityAt), timestampMs(a.createdAt));
  if (activityDiff !== 0) return activityDiff;
  const createdDiff = timestampMs(b.createdAt) - timestampMs(a.createdAt);
  if (createdDiff !== 0) return createdDiff;
  return a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0;
}

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:07:25.668Z

For remote groups, I can pull the explicit project list from the bootstrap settings' PROJECTS value captured at connect time, then build conversation groups using that alongside plans and runs from the snapshot, and finally select the pinned paths from the result.

For identity, I'm using the runner instance id (falling back to profile id) as the scope key, since pins are persisted per profile in the profile store's scoped state. To enumerate all pins across runners, I'd iterate the registry connections and read each profile's pinned projects from scoped state, subscribing to both the profile store and registry for updates. Following the architecture guidance to centralize state, I'm planning a small pinned-projects module in the runners interface that exposes helpers to read pinned project entries from scoped state and to pin a project.

Still writing the pin/unpin helpers and building a pure function that assembles pinned sidebar groups from connections, active profile, and active groups, returning entries with group, profile id, runner name, whether it's the active runner, and pinned timestamp.

For the UI, I'm thinking of placing a pin button in the project header's hover actions, using an icon resembling a pushpin, with "Pin project"/"Unpin project" tooltips—mirroring how chat rows show a hover pin icon. Since the vscode surface has no registry context, pins would simply be disabled there by checking for a null optional registry context.

I'm now working out spacing math for the project header row—accounting for the extra pin button among the existing drag handle, folder icon, name, chevron, add button, and menu button—and recalculating the fixed spacer width used to align chevrons across rows, since the "other" pseudo-group can't be pinned and needs consistent alignment with rows that have three hover buttons instead of two.

For the Projects tab, I'm planning a "Pinned" section at the top, where each pinned group shows like a normal project group but with a filled pin icon instead of a folder icon.

For groups belonging to remote servers, I'll show a small runner badge next to the name, and limit header actions to unpin and a "new conversation" option that switches the active server and starts a draft rather than exposing preset commands (which would execute against the wrong server). For runs shown within a remote pinned group, clicking should switch runners and select that run, but I need to disable rename/archive/delete since those dropdown actions hit the active runtime's APIs directly.

Status indicators get tricky too since read markers seem to be stored per active runner, so for remote rows I'll just surface spinner/awaiting-user icons from run.status and skip the unread dot. For collapse state, I'm debating whether to key it purely by project path (simple but shared across servers with matching paths) or scope it per-server, and leaning toward just reusing the path key for simplicity even though it's slightly imprecise.

Rather than reimplementing the group list from scratch, I'll extend ConversationProjectGroupList with new props for per-group pin state and remote metadata — things like a pinned paths set, a toggle-pin callback, and an onSelectRun override so it can handle both active and remote runner groups.

For remote pinned groups, instead of a separate component I'll make the list generic: each group can carry optional remote info (runner name, profile id), and when present the row skips the menu and unread logic and routes clicks to a remote-select handler. I'm defining a PinnedSidebarGroup type combining the key, profileId, runnerName, isActiveRunner flag, and the underlying group data, then sketching how the sidebar's projects tab would render the pinned groups list.

Since ordering needs to interleave across servers by pin time, I realize the list component itself needs to handle mixed local/remote groups rather than treating them separately, so I'm reworking the approach to extract a single-group renderer as its own component that accepts a group plus remote/pinned flags, making the list just map over mixed items.

Defining drag props and data for the component...

Actually, I'm reconsidering whether to pass a bundled drag handlers object versus restructuring the list as a unified array of items with pinned/remote metadata attached to each group entry, which might simplify the prop surface overall.

I'm deciding to extend the group type itself with extra fields like a unique pin key and remote profile info, rather than using a separate identity-keyed map, so the list can derive React keys and remote handling directly from each group object.

Since pinned groups always move to a separate top section, regular list items never need "pinned" state—they just show a "Pin" action while the pinned section always shows "Unpin." So I'm simplifying the component API to a single toggle callback plus a boolean flag indicating whether the list being rendered is the pinned section, letting the PinnedProjectGroup type carry the extra metadata only there.

For the data flow, I'm thinking the pinned-group computation should live in a custom hook consumed by ConversationSidebar, subscribing to the runner registry context and profile store so it can filter out active-runner pinned paths from the main project list. Since the hook lives inside the sidebar component, registry updates should only trigger re-renders there rather than propagating further up.

But this raises a performance concern: every SSE frame from any runner causes a registry publish, which would re-render the sidebar constantly. To avoid that, I'm considering building a dedicated `PinnedProjectsManager` state manager that subscribes to profileStore and the registry, derives the pins and remote groups, and only publishes when the structural result actually changes.

I'll keep the implementation straightforward: the manager exposes a snapshot of pinned entries, each carrying profile/scope/path/status and an optional sidebar group built from the runner's connection snapshot, plus pin/unpin/isPinned methods for managing pinned state.

For opening conversations, I need handlers for switching to a profile's run or starting a new one against a path — for the active runner these map to existing local handlers, while remote ones go through the registry's switch-active logic. If a remote runner is offline or never connected, I'll still render its pinned group using the path as a fallback name, with an empty run list and some kind of offline indicator; clicking into it would trigger a switch and show the recovery shell, which seems acceptable. I also need search filtering to apply consistently across these remote groups just as it does for the active one.

I'm extracting a shared `filterConversationGroups` helper so both the active and remote paths reuse the same filtering logic, and working out how to reconstruct pinned groups for remote servers — building them from explicit project lists, falling back to an empty group keyed by path/basename when no match exists (unless actively searching), and ordering everything by pin time across servers. Remote run rows will skip unread-state computation since that depends on local message tracking.

Now I'm tracing through the URL sync mechanism when switching active runners: replacing the browser history state to the new run's URL, then calling switchActive, and checking whether the old HomeApp's unmount could race with writing a stale URL before the new one mounts and applies its own bootstrap guard.

The URL already holds routing intent, so buildConversationPath dropping `?runner=` shouldn't matter since ActiveRunnerApp waits for the remote connection to come online before mounting HomeApp. I should also make sure mobile nav closes on selection by setting homeUiSetters.setMobileNav(false) before switching runners.

For actually implementing the remote open, I'm wary of touching selectedRunId on the old HomeApp before switching — that risks a race where it tries to load a nonexistent run on server A and clears/replaces the URL before unmounting. Safer to leave selectedRunId alone, just replace the URL, close the mobile nav, and switch the active runner, though I need to check whether the old HomeApp's URL-sync effect would still fire from the state change.

I'm now thinking the switch-and-open logic belongs in PinnedProjectsManager as an `openRun(profileId, runId)` function: if already active, return false and let the caller handle the local case; otherwise replace browser state and switch active. It's a bit odd having history/window side effects inside a manager, but workable.

I'm checking the persisted pin format in scoped preferences — an array of `{ path, pinnedAt }` — and confirming that `updateScopedState` merges preferences shallowly, so passing just `pinnedProjects` replaces that key cleanly via the registry's merge logic. I need to guard against `scopeKey` throwing when the profile is missing, and I'm noting that `updateScopedState` cascades into a persist, profileStore update, registry reconcile, and publish, which the manager subscribes to.

For the VS Code surface without a registry, pins are unavailable, so I'll just hide pin buttons there. On the main projects list, pinned projects should be removed from view but left untouched in the Active tab. For "Collapse all," I need to include pinned group paths when on the projects tab so they collapse too, and for mobile scroll centering, I'll make sure the sidebar's content key computation accounts for pinned groups alongside the regular visible project groups.

I'm now thinking about where the pinned projects manager actually lives — probably instantiated via the runner registry context, but adding a new prop there changes the provider's API and breaks existing tests. Instead, I could create it lazily using a WeakMap keyed by registry, or build it inside the provider with useMemo from the registry and profile store, exposing it through context with proper start/stop lifecycle in an effect — that approach seems cleanest.

For the remote entry display, I'm deciding to show the runner name as a small badge next to the project name, using a tooltip for status messages, but only showing the badge on groups belonging to other servers rather than all pinned groups, since that's clearer when multiple servers exist.

For remote run rows, interactions are mostly disabled except clicking to open the run and showing a status spinner — rename, dropdown menu, and archive are all hidden. New remote conversations go through a helper that updates the URL and switches the active state. For remote pinned groups, I'm simplifying the context menu to just an unpin option with hover-based pin and add buttons, keeping a spacer for alignment where the "..." menu would normally go, and now working through the overall header layout for local versus remote groups.

I'm settling on using lucide's Pin and PinOff icons, confirming both exist in the version available, matching the style shown in the screenshot where pin appears on hover with a tooltip, though the screenshot example pins chats rather than projects as intended here.

I'll use the existing Tooltip component instead of a plain `title` attribute to match the screenshot's styling, with labels like "Pin project" and "Unpin project," and I'm drafting the needed i18n keys for pinned sections, pin/unpin actions, and a possible server badge label.

export type StateUpdate<T> = T | ((current: T) => T);
export type StateListener = () => void;

export class StateManager<TState> {
  private state: TState;
  private readonly initialState: TState;
  private readonly listeners = new Set<StateListener>();

  constructor(initialState: TState) {
    this.state = initialState;
    this.initialState = initialState;
  }

  getSnapshot() {
    return this.state;
  }

  getInitialSnapshot() {
    return this.initialState;
  }

  subscribe(listener: StateListener) {
    this.listeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      this.listeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  update(updater: StateUpdate<TState>, notify = true) {
    const nextState = typeof updater === "function"
      ? (updater as (current: TState) => TState)(this.state)
      : updater;

    if (Object.is(nextState, this.state)) {
      return this.state;
    }

    this.state = nextState;
    if (notify) {
      this.listeners.forEach((listener) => listener());
    }
    return this.state;
  }

  patch(patch: Partial<TState> | ((current: TState) => Partial<TState>), notify = true) {
    return this.update((current) => ({
      ...current,
      ...(typeof patch === "function" ? patch(current) : patch),
    }), notify);
  }

  setKey<TKey extends keyof TState>(key: TKey, value: StateUpdate<TState[TKey]>, notify = true) {
    return this.update((current) => {
      const nextValue = typeof value === "function"
        ? (value as (currentValue: TState[TKey]) => TState[TKey])(current[key])
        : value;

      if (Object.is(nextValue, current[key])) {
        return current;
      }

      return {
        ...current,
        [key]: nextValue,
      };
    }, notify);
  }
}

"use client";

import { useCallback, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import type { StateManager } from "@/lib/state-manager";

export function useManagerSnapshot<TState>(manager: StateManager<TState>) {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getSnapshot(), [manager]),
    useCallback(() => manager.getInitialSnapshot(), [manager]),
  );
}

export function shallowEqualRecord<TRecord extends Record<string, unknown>>(
  left: TRecord,
  right: TRecord,
) {
  if (Object.is(left, right)) {
    return true;
  }

  const leftKeys = Object.keys(left);
  const rightKeys = Object.keys(right);
  if (leftKeys.length !== rightKeys.length) {
    return false;
  }

  return leftKeys.every((key) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(right, key)
    && Object.is(left[key], right[key]));
}

export function useManagerSelector<TState, TSelected>(
  manager: StateManager<TState>,
  selector: (state: TState) => TSelected,
  isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean = Object.is,
) {
  const selectionRef = useRef<{
    state: TState;
    manager: StateManager<TState>;
    selector: (state: TState) => TSelected;
    isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean;
    selection: TSelected;
  } | null>(null);
  const serverSelectionRef = useRef<{
    state: TState;
    manager: StateManager<TState>;
    selector: (state: TState) => TSelected;
    isEqual: (left: TSelected, right: TSelected) => boolean;
    selection: TSelected;
  } | null>(null);

  const getSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
    const state = manager.getSnapshot();
    const previous = selectionRef.current;
    if (
      previous?.state === state
      && previous.manager === manager
      && previous.selector === selector
      && previous.isEqual === isEqual
    ) {
      return previous.selection;
    }

    const nextSelection = selector(state);
    if (previous && isEqual(previous.selection, nextSelection)) {
      selectionRef.current = {
        state,
        manager,
        selector,
        isEqual,
        selection: previous.selection,
      };
      return previous.selection;
    }

    selectionRef.current = {
      state,
      manager,
      selector,
      isEqual,
      selection: nextSelection,
    };
    return nextSelection;
  }, [isEqual, manager, selector]);
  const getServerSelectedSnapshot = useCallback(() => {
    const state = manager.getInitialSnapshot();
    const previous = serverSelectionRef.current;
    if (
      previous?.state === state
      && previous.manager === manager
      && previous.selector === selector
      && previous.isEqual === isEqual
    ) {
      return previous.selection;
    }
    const selection = selector(state);
    serverSelectionRef.current = { state, manager, selector, isEqual, selection };
    return selection;
  }, [isEqual, manager, selector]);

  return useSyncExternalStore(
    useCallback((listener) => manager.subscribe(listener), [manager]),
    getSelectedSnapshot,
    getServerSelectedSnapshot,
  );
}

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:09:26.599Z

I need to cast ConversationGroup to SidebarGroup since the optional mode and preferredWorkerType fields align fine. I'll extract the pinned groups search filter logic into a shared `filterConversationGroupsBySearch` function in conversations.ts, rather than keeping it inline in useHomeViewModel, so it can be reused.

Now I'm sketching out the sidebar restructuring: ConversationProjectGroupList should take a list of items, each bundling the group, pinned state, an optional remote source descriptor, and a toggle-pin closure, built via useMemo in ConversationSidebar so each call site constructs items from its filtered groups.

I'm working through how pinned entries resolve back to actual project groups—matching by path against the active server's filtered projects, and handling the edge case where a pinned project was removed from the active server's list, needing either a skip during search or a placeholder group.

For remote pinned entries, I'm filtering the remote group by search query and wiring up its run data—runner name, status, read markers—plus an openRun handler that calls into the manager to open the run for that profile. I also need to handle mobile nav: closing the drawer when a remote run is opened on mobile, mirroring how local run selection already closes the nav.

I'm settling on using `onCollapse` conditionally only in mobile mode rather than importing UI setters directly into ConversationSidebar. Since remote run IDs are UUIDs from a different server, there's no risk of collision with local selected run highlighting, and pinning should remain disabled for the "other" group, with collapse-all including pinned item paths. Now I'm writing the rendering logic for pinned items in the projects tab.

I'll place it at the top of the Projects tab list with a small "Pinned" label and a subtle divider separating pinned from the rest. For each group's header row, I'm adding a pin/unpin toggle button with tooltip alongside the existing actions.

Let me check how Tooltip with render is used elsewhere in the sidebar to copy that same pattern, and keep hover visibility behavior consistent with existing items rather than adding extra focus-visible handling. I also need to make sure the remote project name displays properly alongside its server badge.

I'm working out the layout math for the action button groups -- figuring out spacer widths for the "other" group now that a pin button is being added alongside the existing buttons, making sure the gaps and widths stay consistent across groups with two versus three buttons.

For remote run rows, I'm wiring up click handlers to open and read runs remotely, disabling rename/archive/dropdown for remote sessions, and resolving unread state from remote read markers instead of local ones. I'm also checking that the show-more button and collapsible session groups still work correctly with remote paths.

I'm confirming the empty-state logic for project group lists stays correct when groups are populated, and rethinking how the sidebar's scroll key should account for pinned items by computing it from all rendered items together. For pin permissions, I need the active runner ID from the registry's state manager via a selector hook, but I'm wary of conditional hook usage since the active runner can change and cause remounts.

For cases where context is null, I'll set up module-level fallback state managers. Pinning a project that isn't pinned yet requires the active profile ID, which I'll pull through a selector. Now I'm moving on to writing the filter helper function in conversations.ts.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:09:41.229Z

I'm planning the sidebar edits: adding new icon imports and context hooks for runner registry and pinned projects, plus bringing in search filtering and runner status utilities so the component can support pinning and connection status display.

I'm defining types for a remote project source (runner name, status, read markers, run/conversation actions) and a project group list item combining the group, pin state, and remote info—deciding to store raw status and translate it at render time rather than inside the memoized item builder. Then I'm updating the conversation project group list component to accept these new items instead of plain groups, and moving on to rework the list body itself.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:10:21.347Z

I'm pulling in the pinned projects manager from the runner registry context and snapshotting its entries to compute which items should appear in the sidebar.

Now I'm working through a type mismatch: the active runner ID selector needs a consistent StateManager type whether or not a real registry context exists, so I'll make the fallback NO_RUNNER_REGISTRY fully typed with all required fields rather than a partial, and similarly ensure the pinned projects fallback resolves cleanly to a single StateManager type.

Building the pinned project items list...

Still wiring up pinned item handlers...

I'm mapping projects and active groups into item lists with pin-toggle handlers, then deciding visibleItems should combine pinned and regular project items when on the projects tab versus just active items otherwise, since this drives collapse-all behavior and the sidebar content key.

These derived hooks need to stay above the early mounted-check return, so I'll place visibleProjectGroups near the top of the component alongside the other hooks.

export async function startRunnerSet(
  names: string[],
  options: { bypassAuth?: boolean } = {},

    for (const [index, name] of names.entries()) {

        name,

        bypassAuth: options.bypassAuth,

      await runner.start();
    }
    return runners;
  } catch (error) {
    await Promise.all(runners.map((runner) => runner.dispose()));
    throw error;
  }
}

export async function disposeRunnerSet(runners: RealRunnerHarness[]) {
  for (const runner of runners) {
    runner.assertNoSecretLogs();
  }
  await Promise.all(runners.map((runner) => runner.dispose()));
}
import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import {
  RealRunnerHarness,
  disposeRunnerSet,
  startRunnerSet,
} from "./multi-runner-harness";

test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

let runners: RealRunnerHarness[] = [];

async function login(page: Page, runner: RealRunnerHarness) {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.localStorage.setItem("omni.onboarding.seen", "1");
  });
  await page.goto(runner.origin);
  await page.locator("#omni-password").fill(runner.options.password);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Unlock OmniHarness" }).click();
  await expect(page.locator("#runner-switcher")).toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });
  const setup = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Finish CLI setup" });
  if (await setup.isVisible().catch(() => false)) {
    await setup.getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }).click();
  }
}

async function connectRunner(
  page: Page,
  runner: RealRunnerHarness,
) {
  await page.locator("#runner-switcher").click();
  await page.getByText("Add runner", { exact: true }).click();
  await page.locator("#runner-label").fill(runner.options.name);
  await page.locator("#runner-url").fill(runner.origin);
  const popupPromise = page.waitForEvent("popup");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Connect", exact: true }).click();
  const popup = await popupPromise;
  await popup.locator("#authorization-password").fill(runner.options.password);
  await popup.getByRole("button", { name: "Authorize", exact: true }).click();
  await popup.waitForEvent("close");
  await expect.poll(async () => {
    const switcher = page.locator("#runner-switcher");
    const count = await switcher.count();
    return {
      count,
      name: count ? await switcher.getAttribute("aria-label") : null,
      body: (await page.locator("body").innerText()).slice(0, 500),
      url: page.url(),
    };
  }, { timeout: 30_000 }).toMatchObject({
    count: 1,
    name: expect.stringContaining(runner.options.name),
  });
}

async function selectRunner(page: Page, name: string) {
  await page.locator("#runner-switcher").click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem").filter({ hasText: name }).first().click();
  await expect(page.locator("#runner-switcher")).toHaveAccessibleName(
    new RegExp(name),
  );
}

test.beforeAll(async () => {
  runners = await startRunnerSet(["Runner One", "Runner Two"]);
});

test.afterAll(async () => {
  await disposeRunnerSet(runners);
  runners = [];
});

test("automatically unlocks the current server with its saved password after reload", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  const [first] = runners;
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.localStorage.setItem("omni.onboarding.seen", "1");
  });
  await page.goto(first.origin);
  await expect(page.locator("#omni-password")).toBeVisible();

  await page.locator("#runner-switcher").click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: /Edit connection/ }).click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Edit server" });
  await dialog.locator("#runner-password").fill(first.options.password);
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Connect", exact: true }).click();

  await expect(page.locator("#omni-password")).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });
  await expect(page.locator("#runner-switcher")).toHaveAccessibleName(/Online/);

  await page.context().clearCookies();
  await page.reload();

  await expect(page.locator("#omni-password")).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 30_000 });
  await expect(page.locator("#runner-switcher")).toHaveAccessibleName(/Online/);
});

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:13:54.221Z

I'm thinking through how to create a conversation on the second runner for testing—settings merged fine, but spawning a run will kick off processes in the temp root, and disposal will kill the runner once done. I'll accept that tradeoff and try a planning-mode run with the mock LLM to keep it lightweight.

Now I'm sketching an e2e test for pinned projects: seeding each runner's settings with its projects, creating a run on runner two, logging in and connecting to runner two, then pinning the beta project and verifying it stays visible.

Continuing, I'm checking that switching to runner one still shows beta-project pinned with a "Runner Two" badge while alpha-project appears in the regular list, then clicking the pinned remote run to confirm it switches the active runner, updates the URL, and persists after a reload before testing unpin behavior.

The title may come from MOCK_LLM generation, so I need to verify the selected row gets marked with its highlight class rather than relying on aria-current, which isn't present. For creating conversations via API I'll need to include an origin header for CSRF alongside the session cookie, following the harness pattern, and I'm setting up a separate test config with an absolute testDir path that skips the webServer since runner names might otherwise collide with other multi-runner specs.

I'm weighing whether to reuse the existing dev server or spin up a new one — starting another pnpm dev instance seems wasteful, but putting a temporary config in /tmp risks module resolution issues with @playwright/test. I'm leaning toward writing the config directly in the repo so dependency resolution works correctly.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:19:46.101Z

This looks decent overall. The pinned project rows after pinning Runner Two lose the grip indent compared to regular projects, which is fine, and runs keep consistent indentation; the remote run row has no "..." menu but its "+" button works, and the unread sky dot correctly marks the never-read run.

Checking a few more things: remote hover correctly shows unpin, plus, and spacer; the "No conversations" state for alpha-project is hidden behind, which is fine; and the hover in the first screenshot places the pin icon between chevron and plus, matching the requested style, with the "Pinned" header showing its small pin icon as expected. For remaining considerations, mobile buttons stay visible with opacity-100 below the lg breakpoint, which could crowd three buttons plus a badge but seems acceptable, and I should keep the e2e spec in the repo as a valid regression test alongside the multi-runner spec, though the existing multi-runner spec references a stale "Add runner" label that's outside my scope. I'm also confirming that when the remote server is offline, the group derived from the stale snapshot still lets clicking switch to a recovery shell correctly, and that in the VS Code surface without registry context, pin buttons are properly hidden since the pinned projects manager is null. Now I'm looking at how `handleRemoveProject` in HomeApp handles this case.

If a user removes a pinned active project, the pin would remain and show a placeholder group with no runs, which seems surprising -- so I should make removing a project also unpin it, wrapping the handler passed to the lists so that if the removed path is the pinned one, it unpins as well. I'm also confirming `filteredProjects` logic works the same for remote groups and that the registry type passed to `useManagerSelector` typechecks correctly. Time to implement the remove-then-unpin behavior.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T18:22:02.159Z

Everything's clean now, no leftover test servers or temp roots, and nothing was created on the user's real server since the run was isolated. I'm preparing a concise final summary covering the design decisions: a pin icon appearing on hover of the project header with a tooltip, an unpin option, and a pinned section at the top of the Projects tab ordered by pin time, with pinned projects excluded from the regular list.

For projects from other servers, I'll note the server-name badge, how clicking switches server context, and that rename/archive/delete actions are hidden on remote rows since they'd act on the wrong server. I should also flag the storage trade-off — pins are stored per-browser/device and not synced, so forgetting a server drops its pins — plus mention that remote project lists reflect settings from connection time. I'll note this isn't committed yet, summarize test results (unit, e2e with two real servers, typecheck, lint, build, with 11 pre-existing unrelated failures), and briefly flag the stale "Add runner" label in the existing multi-runner spec as a minor aside worth mentioning.

## Claude · 2026-10-26T18:22:03.601Z

Pinning works, including across servers. I checked it end to end against two real isolated test servers: pin a project on server two, switch to server one, and the project is still at the top. Clicking one of its conversations switches to server two and opens it.

**How it behaves**
- **Pin icon:** hovering a project header shows a pin button next to `+`, with a tooltip like "Pin virals". Pinned projects show an unpin icon instead. It's lucide's `Pin`/`PinOff`, which matches your screenshot.
- **Pinned section:** pinned projects move into a "Pinned" section at the top of the Projects tab, in the order you pinned them, and no longer appear twice in the list below.
- **Projects on other servers** show a small server-name badge.
  - Clicking one of their conversations switches to that server and opens it. `+` starts a new conversation in that project on that server.
  - Rename, archive, delete and move are hidden on those rows, because they would act on the server currently selected.
- Removing a project also unpins it.

**Decision for you:** pins are saved in the browser/app, keyed by server, not on the servers themselves. That's what lets one list span all servers, but pins don't sync between devices: pinning on your laptop won't pin on your phone. Forgetting a server drops its pins. If you want them to sync, each server would have to store its own pins; say if you want that.

One smaller limitation: for a project on a server that isn't selected, its conversations update live, but the project list itself comes from when that server last connected.

**Verification**
- Added an end-to-end test (`tests/e2e/pinned-projects.spec.ts`) using the repo's two-server test setup, plus unit tests for the pin logic. Both pass.
- Typecheck, lint and `pnpm build:interface:web` pass. I updated four existing tests that check exact source text I changed.
- The full unit suite has 11 failures (worker models, CORS, port cutover, among others). The same 11 fail with my changes removed.
- No test conversations were created on your real server. The test servers and their temp data were cleaned up.
- The existing `tests/e2e/multi-runner.spec.ts` looks for an "Add runner" menu item, which the UI now labels "Add server". I used the new label in my test and left that spec alone.

The main pieces are a new `src/interface/runners/PinnedProjectsManager.ts` and changes in `src/components/home/ConversationSidebar.tsx`, plus the new strings in all nine locale files. Nothing is committed.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T23:00:23.703Z

The user wants two things: pinning individual chat sessions with a hover pin icon showing "Pin chat" tooltip and pinned sessions appearing at the top across servers, and keeping project pins but adding a machine name label with a status dot on the right side of each project row to show which server it's on and whether it's online.

For sessions, I'm planning to store pinned entries as a list with run IDs and timestamps in the same scoped preferences, then compute entries by matching each pinned run against its connection's snapshot — tracking profile, runner name, status, active state, and the underlying run data. The sidebar would then surface a "Pinned" section at the top showing these flattened rows, similar to how another app displays its pinned items.

I'm deciding to show the machine name right-aligned in muted text on pinned session rows too, since knowing which server a session lives on seems just as useful there as for projects. So the layout becomes: pinned sessions first, then pinned projects with machine name and status dot, then the regular project list below.

To avoid duplicates, pinned sessions should be filtered out of their regular project groups (and from pinned project groups) across the Projects tab, while the Recent tab stays unchanged. Each session row needs a hover pin icon alongside the archive control, with pin/unpin tooltips, and pin toggling for remote sessions should work fine since it's handled client-side through the manager with a profileId — I just need to extract the row rendering logic so it can be reused for the new flat pinned-session list.

I'm restructuring this into a dedicated row component that takes props for the run data, selection state, unread status, an optional remote-open handler, pin state with a toggle, and optional machine label info.

Rather than passing a long list of individual callbacks (select, rename, move, archive, delete), I'm bundling them into a single actions object type that the list builds once and passes down, keeping the component API cleaner while preserving the existing list-level props.

I also need to generalize the manager to use a `pinnedSessions` preferences key, and reconstruct a SidebarRun-shaped object for pinned entries by flattening the cached conversation groups into a runId lookup map. For active-server pins with no run reference, I should find the matching run in local filteredProjects; if it's missing entirely (deleted), I'll just skip rendering it rather than show a broken entry, and make sure deleteRun also unpins the session so it doesn't linger in storage.

Similarly archiving a pinned run should unpin it too, so I'll wrap archiveRun the same way. If a remote pinned session's server is offline with no cached snapshot, I'll just skip rendering it. Pinned sessions should also respect the search filter by matching title/path, and I'm now weighing whether showing a machine label makes sense when there's only a single configured server, since repeating the same name on every row feels like unnecessary noise.

For the status dot itself, I'll use green for online, amber for connecting/resyncing, and a muted red or gray for offline, pulling the existing color scheme from RunnerControls' status indicators for consistency.

7	/**

9	 * one server's settings: a pinned project stays reachable while a different

11	 * scope is the server identity, so a pin follows the server across profile

Null for the active server. */\n  group: ConversationGroup | null;\n};\n\nexport type PinnedSessionEntry = PinnedEntryBase & {\n  runId: string;\n  /**\n   * From that server's own live snapshot. Null for the active server, and for\n   * a run the server no longer reports.\n   */\n  run: ConversationGroupRun | null;\n};\n\nexport type PinnedItemsSnapshot = {\n  projects: PinnedProjectEntry[];\n  sessions: PinnedSessionEntry[];\n  /** Pins only say which machine they belong to when there is more than one. */\n  serverCount: number;\n};\n\ntype PinnedItemsProfileStore = {\n  getSnapshot(): RunnerProfileStoreSnapshot;\n  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;\n  getScopedState(profileId: string): RunnerScopedState;\n  updateScopedState(profileId: string, patch: Partial<RunnerScopedState>): Promise<void>;\n};\n\ntype PinnedItemsRegistry = {\n  getSnapshot(): { activeRunnerId: string | null; connections: RunnerConnectionSnapshot[] };\n  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;\n  switchActive(profileId: string): boolean;\n};\n\ntype RemoteCatalogCache = {\n  snapshot: Record<string, unknown> | null;\n  projectsSetting: string | undefined;\n  groups: ConversationGroup[];\n  runsById: Map<string, ConversationGroupRun>;\n  /** Pinned paths the server reports nothing for still need a stable group. */\n  placeholders: Map<string, ConversationGroup>;\n};\n\nconst NO_READ_MARKERS: Record<string, string> = {};\n\nfunction readRecords<T extends { pinnedAt: string }>(\n  value: unknown,\n  readId: (item: Record<string, unknown>) => string | null,\n  build: (id: string, pinnedAt: string) => T,\n): T[] {\n  if (!Array.isArray(value)) {\n    return [];\n  }\n  const seen = new Set<string>();\n  const records: T[] = [];\n  for (const item of value) {\n    if (!item || typeof item !== \"object\") continue;\n    const id = readId(item as Record<string, unknown>);\n    if (!id || seen.has(id)) continue;\n    seen.add(id);\n    const pinnedAt = (item as { pinnedAt?: unknown }).pinnedAt;\n    records.push(build(id, typeof pinnedAt === \"string\" ? pinnedAt : \"\"));\n  }\n  return records;\n}\n\nexport function readPinnedProjects(preferences: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): PinnedProjectRecord[] {\n  return readRecords(\n    preferences?.[PINNED_PROJECTS_PREFERENCE_KEY],\n    (item) => (typeof item.path === \"string\" && item.path.trim() ? normalizeProjectPath(item.path) : null),\n    (path, pinnedAt) => ({ path, pinnedAt }),\n  );\n}\n\nexport function readPinnedSessions(preferences: Record<string, unknown> | undefined): PinnedSessionRecord[] {\n  return readRecords(\n    preferences?.[PINNED_SESSIONS_PREFERENCE_KEY],\n    (item) => (typeof item.runId === \"string\" && item.runId.trim() ? item.runId.trim() : null),\n    (runId, pinnedAt) => ({ runId, pinnedAt }),\n  );\n}\n\nfunction parseProjectsSetting(value: string | undefined) {\n  if (!value?.trim()) return [];\n  try {\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(value);\n    return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed.filter((entry): entry is string => typeof entry === \"string\") : [];\n  } catch {\n    return [];\n  }\n}\n\nfunction asArray<T>(value: unknown) {\n  return Array.isArray(value) ? value as T[] : [];\n}\n\nfunction byPinnedAt(left: { pinnedAt: string }, right: { pinnedAt: string }) {\n  return left.pinnedAt < right.pinnedAt ? -1 : left.pinnedAt > right.pinnedAt ? 1 : 0;\n}\n\nfunction sameBase(entry: PinnedEntryBase, other: PinnedEntryBase) {\n  return entry.key === other.key\n    && entry.runnerName === other.runnerName\n    && entry.status === other.status\n    && entry.active === other.active\n    && entry.pinnedAt === other.pinnedAt\n    && entry.readMarkers === other.readMarkers;\n}\n\nfunction sameProjects(left: PinnedProjectEntry[], right: PinnedProjectEntry[]) {\n  return left.length === right.length\n    && left.every((entry, index) => sameBase(entry, right[index]!) && entry.group === right[index]!.group);\n}\n\nfunction sameSessions(left: PinnedSessionEntry[], right: PinnedSessionEntry[]) {\n  return left.length === right.length\n    && left.every((entry, index) => sameBase(entry, right[index]!) && entry.run === right[index]!.run);\n}\n\nexport class PinnedItemsManager extends StateManager<PinnedItemsSnapshot> {\n  private readonly registry: PinnedItemsRegistry;\n  private readonly profileStore: PinnedItemsProfileStore;\n  private readonly now: () => string;\n  private readonly replaceUrl: (path: string) => void;\n  private readonly remoteCatalogs = new Map<string, RemoteCatalogCache>();\n  private unsubscribes: Array<() => void> = [];\n\n  constructor(options: {\n    registry: PinnedItemsRegistry;\n    profileStore: PinnedItemsProfileStore;\n    now?: () => string;\n    replaceUrl?: (path: string) => void;\n  }) {\n    super({ projects: [], sessions: [], serverCount: 0 });\n    this.registry = options.registry;\n    this.profileStore = options.profileStore;\n    this.now = options.now ?? (() => new Date().toISOString());\n    this.replaceUrl = options.replaceUrl ?? ((path) => {\n      if (typeof window !== \"undefined\") {\n        window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, \"\", path);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  start() {\n    if (this.unsubscribes.length > 0) return;\n    const recompute = () => this.recompute();\n    this.unsubscribes = [\n      this.registry.subscribe(recompute),\n      this.profileStore.subscribe(recompute),\n    ];\n    this.recompute();\n  }\n\n  stop() {\n    for (const unsubscribe of this.unsubscribes) unsubscribe();\n    this.unsubscribes = [];\n    this.remoteCatalogs.clear();\n  }\n\n  isProjectPinned(profileId: string, path: string) {\n    const normalizedPath = normalizeProjectPath(path);\n    return this.readPreferences(profileId, readPinnedProjects).some((record) => record.path === normalizedPath);\n  }\n\n  isSessionPinned(profileId: string, runId: string) {\n    return this.readPreferences(profileId, readPinnedSessions).some((record) => record.runId === runId);\n  }\n\n  setProjectPinned(profileId: string, path: string, pinned: boolean) {\n    const normalizedPath = normalizeProjectPath(path);\n    return this.writePin(\n      profileId,\n      PINNED_PROJECTS_PREFERENCE_KEY,\n      this.readPreferences(profileId, readPinnedProjects),\n      (record) => record.path === normalizedPath,\n      pinned ? { path: normalizedPath, pinnedAt: this.now() } : null,\n    );\n  }\n\n  setSessionPinned(profileId: string, runId: string, pinned: boolean) {\n    return this.writePin(\n      profileId,\n      PINNED_SESSIONS_PREFERENCE_KEY,\n      this.readPreferences(profileId, readPinnedSessions),\n      (record) => record.runId === runId,\n      pinned ? { runId, pinnedAt: this.now() } : null,\n    );\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Opening a pinned item on another server is a server switch. The route is\n   * written first because the app remounts for the new server and takes its\n   * selection from the URL, exactly as a deep link would.\n   */\n  openRun(profileId: string, runId: string) {\n    this.replaceUrl(`/session/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}`);\n    return this.registry.switchActive(profileId);\n  }\n\n  beginConversation(profileId: string, path: string) {\n    this.replaceUrl(`/?${new URLSearchParams({ project: path }).toString()}`);\n    return this.registry.switchActive(profileId);\n  }\n\n  private async writePin<T>(\n    profileId: string,\n    preferenceKey: string,\n    current: T[],\n    matches: (record: T) => boolean,\n    added: T | null,\n  ) {\n    const without = current.filter((record) => !matches(record));\n    const alreadyPinned = without.length !== current.length;\n    // Re-pinning keeps the original position; unpinning an absent pin is a no-op.\n    if (added ? alreadyPinned : !alreadyPinned) {\n      return;\n    }\n    await this.profileStore.updateScopedState(profileId, {\n      preferences: { [preferenceKey]: added ? [...without, added] : without },\n    });\n  }\n\n  private readPreferences<T>(profileId: string, read: (preferences: Record<string, unknown>) => T[]) {\n    try {\n      return read(this.profileStore.getScopedState(profileId).preferences);\n    } catch {\n      return [];\n    }\n  }\n\n  private remoteCatalogFor(connection: RunnerConnectionSnapshot) {\n    const projectsSetting = connection.bootstrap?.initialQueries?.settings?.values?.PROJECTS;\n    const cached = this.remoteCatalogs.get(connection.profileId);\n    if (cached && cached.snapshot === connection.snapshot && cached.projectsSetting === projectsSetting) {\n      return cached;\n    }\n    const groups = buildConversationGroups({\n      explicitProjects: parseProjectsSetting(projectsSetting),\n      plans: asArray(connection.snapshot?.plans),\n      runs: asArray(connection.snapshot?.runs),\n    });\n    const next: RemoteCatalogCache = {\n      snapshot: connection.snapshot,\n      projectsSetting,\n      groups,\n      runsById: new Map(groups.flatMap((group) => group.runs.map((run) => [run.id, run] as const))),\n      placeholders: cached?.placeholders ?? new Map(),\n    };\n    this.remoteCatalogs.set(connection.profileId, next);\n    return next;\n  }\n\n  private remoteGroupFor(catalog: RemoteCatalogCache, path: string) {\n    const group = catalog.groups.find((candidate) => candidate.path === path);\n    if (group) return group;\n    let placeholder = catalog.placeholders.get(path);\n    if (!placeholder) {\n      placeholder = { path, name: path.split(/[/\\\\]/).pop() || path, runs: [] };\n      catalog.placeholders.set(path, placeholder);\n    }\n    return placeholder;\n  }\n\n  private recompute() {\n    const { activeRunnerId, connections } = this.registry.getSnapshot();\n    const liveProfileIds = new Set(connections.map((connection) => connection.profileId));\n    for (const profileId of this.remoteCatalogs.keys()) {\n      if (!liveProfileIds.has(profileId)) this.remoteCatalogs.delete(profileId);\n    }\n\n    const projects: PinnedProjectEntry[] = [];\n    const sessions: PinnedSessionEntry[] = [];\n    for (const connection of connections) {\n      const projectPins = this.readPreferences(connection.profileId, readPinnedProjects);\n      const sessionPins = this.readPreferences(connection.profileId, readPinnedSessions);\n      if (projectPins.length === 0 && sessionPins.length === 0) continue;\n      const active = connection.profileId === activeRunnerId;\n      const catalog = active ? null : this.remoteCatalogFor(connection);\n      const base = {\n        profileId: connection.profileId,\n        runnerName: connection.runnerName,\n        status: connection.status,\n        active,\n        readMarkers: active\n          ? NO_READ_MARKERS\n          : (connection.snapshot?.readMarkers ?? NO_READ_MARKERS) as Record<string, string>,\n      };\n      for (const pin of projectPins) {\n        projects.push({\n          ...base,\n          key: `${connection.profileId}\\u0000project\\u0000${pin.path}`,\n          pinnedAt: pin.pinnedAt,\n          path: pin.path,\n          group: catalog ? this.remoteGroupFor(catalog, pin.path) : null,\n        });\n      }\n      for (const pin of sessionPins) {\n        sessions.push({\n          ...base,\n          key: `${connection.profileId}\\u0000session\\u0000${pin.runId}`,\n          pinnedAt: pin.pinnedAt,\n          runId: pin.runId,\n          run: catalog?.runsById.get(pin.runId) ?? null,\n        });\n      }\n    }\n    projects.sort(byPinnedAt);\n    sessions.sort(byPinnedAt);\n\n    const current = this.getSnapshot();\n    const serverCount = connections.length;\n    if (\n      current.serverCount !== serverCount\n      || !sameProjects(current.projects, projects)\n      || !sameSessions(current.sessions, sessions)\n    ) {\n      this.update({ projects, sessions, serverCount });\n    }\n  }\n}\n"
}

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T23:01:35.070Z

I'm planning the refactor by defining the key types: a pinned machine with name and connection status, a remote project source holding markers/run/conversation methods, and a project group list item that bundles the key, group, pin state, and optional remote source.

I'm realizing pinned sessions get filtered out of groups in the projects tab (so rows only need a "pin" action), but in the Recent tab pinned sessions stay visible, so I need a session pin interface tracking per-run pinned state and a toggle function. I'm also sketching a ConversationRunRow component with props for selection, unread state, remote opening, session pin, machine info, and a bundle of row actions covering renaming, moving, archiving, and deleting runs.

For layout, I'm placing the machine label (muted name plus a dot) before the chevron in project headers, and before the hover action buttons in session rows, with hover-revealed pin and archive/menu buttons matching the screenshot. I'm deciding the machine label only shows when there's more than one server, applying to both pinned projects and sessions, active or remote.

I need to remove the old remote badge in favor of this new machine label, and make sure both the recent tab and projects tab reflect pin state correctly — pinned sessions should be filtered out of their normal groups while still appearing in pinned sections. I also want deleteRun/archiveRun to unpin a session automatically when it's removed from the active server.

For resolving pinned sessions on the active server, I'm looking up the run by id using the search-filtered project data so it respects the current search state — if a run doesn't match search it stays hidden, and if it's missing entirely (not loaded or deleted) I just skip it.

For remote pinned sessions, I'll filter by matching title or path against the query. For unread state, I need to compute latestMessageAtByRunId consistently for both local and pinned rows, so I'm pulling that logic into a shared hook and a helper function that compares the latest message timestamp against read markers to determine unread status, with the status dot logic staying in the row component which just takes a boolean prop.

Rather than patching piecemeal, I think it's cleaner to rewrite the whole section covering the remote project source type through the end of ConversationProjectGroupList, so I'm reading through the current list body to capture its full structure first.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T23:02:13.942Z

I'm planning to replace the block of code covering the pinned project section with a new implementation, including a component that renders a pinned machine's label based on its connection status.

Still writing component code...

I'm considering renaming the "pinnedProjectServer" locale key to "pinnedMachine" for clarity, which would require updating that key across all locale files via a script. I'm also adding a screen-reader-only text span for the status indicator since the colored dot isn't otherwise accessible.

Now I'm starting to define a type for run row actions, covering selection state, renaming state, and related handlers.

Still writing pin button...

I'm thinking through row layout at narrow sidebar widths, with title truncation handling overflow and the machine label capped at 40% width. For pinned remote sessions, the menu is hidden so the row's less crowded, and I'm weighing whether the group list should keep individual props like `machine` and `sessionPin` or consolidate into a single `actions` prop to minimize call-site churn.

I'm settling on bundling those into a `runRowActions` object built via useMemo in the sidebar, then designing a `PinnedSessionList` that maps items through `ConversationRunRow` inside a labeled section alongside the pinned project groups, keeping indentation consistent between session rows and folder rows. I'm also sketching a small helper function to determine whether a sidebar run should be marked unread based on the latest message.

To avoid duplicating computation, I'm deciding to compute `latestMessageAtByRunId` once in the sidebar and pass it into the list instead of passing raw messages, replacing the `messages` prop entirely. Now I'm defining the shape of each project group list item.

Adding header elements...

Still wiring up pin state...

Building the pinned row items...

I need to double-check: a local pinned run might still live inside its project group in filteredProjects, and whether that group might get filtered out entirely elsewhere needs verifying.

For remote sessions, matching search is just a case-insensitive check against title or path. For remote project groups, I need to exclude runs that are pinned for that profile, using a per-profile set of pinned run IDs, and build the pin toggle so it calls setSessionPinned with the right true/false state. The Recent tab reuses local pin state without extra filtering, and pinned sessions should surface at the top in Projects regardless of which tab.

I'll keep the Pinned section (sessions + projects) visible only in the Projects tab, while Recent still shows pin state inline within its groups. Pinned project items get machine info when showMachines is enabled, while regular items get null; delete/archive actions get wrapped to also unpin locally; I'm adding a "Pinned" section header, adjusting empty-state logic, updating sidebarContentKey to include pinned keys, limiting collapse-all to projects, and adding new i18n keys for pin/unpin session tooltips.

I'll simplify the tooltip and aria-label to just "Pin session"/"Unpin session" rather than including the title, rename pinnedProjectServer to pinnedMachine, and add translations for these labels across German, Spanish, French, Italian, and Japanese.

With the remaining Korean, Portuguese, and Chinese translations added, I'm ready to start writing the code.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T23:06:53.780Z

I'm noticing the hover action buttons in the project header still take up layout space even when invisible on large screens, which squeezes the project name and machine name together. I should switch those buttons to use `hidden` combined with `group-hover:flex` instead of opacity, so they don't reserve space when not shown.

On the swap behavior, I'll have the machine label hide on hover while actions appear in its place, giving a clean transition rather than squeezing text. For mobile widths, I'll leave both visible since there's less hover interaction to worry about there.

I'm also noting that session rows show a machine label plus dot that squeezes the title text, when the reference design doesn't show machine info at that level at all—likely because machine context belongs on the project row, not duplicated on every pinned session.

I'm weighing whether to stack the machine label under the title on a second line for pinned sessions, versus applying the same hover-swap trick there too, and I realize the existing opacity-0 action buttons already waste horizontal space in every row — though I'll only touch that for rows that actually have machine labels, to keep the change scoped. For implementation, I'm wrapping the pin/archive/menu buttons so they're hidden until hover or focus-within when a machine label exists, and hiding the machine label itself on hover/focus-within — though I need to double check this doesn't break once a dropdown menu opens and the mouse leaves the row area, since the portal content won't preserve the hover state.

An overlay approach with absolutely positioned icons over the timestamp seems too finicky with background matching, so I'll stick with the display-swap idea but keep the trigger rendered while the menu is open using the `has-[[data-popup-open]]` selector, since Base UI's Menu.Trigger does set that attribute when active.

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-26T23:07:01.283Z

I'm confirming that Tailwind v4 supports `has-data-*` variants, so I can use `group-has-data-popup-open:flex` on the group row divs to show elements when the popup is open, since the group classes are correctly placed on the header and run rows without nested conflicts.

I'm defining swap classes for machine label and actions that hide/show on hover, focus, or popup-open at the `lg` breakpoint, then applying them to the pin/archive/menu buttons in run rows and to the project header's action container alongside the machine label. For focus handling, I'm switching from `group-focus-within` to `group-has-focus-visible` so the swap only persists for keyboard focus rather than lingering awkwardly after a mouse click collapses a pinned project.

## Claude · 2026-10-26T23:09:57.144Z

Sessions can now be pinned, and every pinned item shows which machine it lives on, laid out like your screenshot: name on the left, machine name and a status dot on the right. I checked it in a real browser against two isolated test servers, in light and dark mode.

**Pinned sessions**
- Hovering any session row shows a pin icon with a "Pin session" tooltip, like your first screenshot.
- Pinned sessions go to the top of the "Pinned" section, above pinned projects, and leave their project group so they don't appear twice.
- They work across servers. A session pinned on Runner Two stays visible while Runner One is selected, and clicking it switches to Runner Two and opens it.
- Deleting or archiving a pinned session also unpins it.
- On the Recent tab, sessions stay where they are and the pin icon just shows whether each one is pinned.

**Machine labels**
- Pinned projects and sessions show the machine name with a status dot: green when online, amber while connecting, red when offline.
- On desktop, hovering a row swaps the label for the pin/`+`/`…` buttons. The hidden buttons had still been taking up width, which cut both names to "gamma… Run…"; now both read in full.
- I left out the small globe badge on the folder icon from your screenshot.

**Decisions for you**
- The machine label only appears when more than one server is configured, since a single server has nothing to tell apart. If you want it shown always, it's a one-line change.
- As before, pins are saved per device (browser/app), not on the servers, so they don't sync between your laptop and phone.

**Verification**
- Typecheck, lint and the web build pass.
- The unit tests for pin logic pass (now in `tests/interface/runners/pinned-items-manager.test.ts`).
- The two-server end-to-end spec passes. It's now `tests/e2e/pinned-items.spec.ts`, with a second scenario for pinned sessions.
- The full unit suite has the same 11 failures it had before any of my changes, all in server and script tests.
- One leftover test folder from a test server's temp directory was removed. No test servers are still running.

The pin logic is now `src/interface/runners/PinnedItemsManager.ts`, replacing last turn's `PinnedProjectsManager`. Session rows were pulled out into one shared component in `ConversationSidebar.tsx`. Nothing is committed.

No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {\"kind\":\"project\",\"create\":{\"name\":\"<title>\",\"doc\":{\"blocks\":{\"asof\":{\"type\":\"date\",\"value\":\"<today>\"},\"me\":{\"type\":\"mention\",\"user\":\"me\"},\"s1\":{\"type\":\"pending\",\"intent\":\"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to\"},\"s2\":{…}},\"markdown\":\"# <title>\\n\\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\\n\\n<?claude block s1?>\\n\\n<?claude block s2?>\"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = [\"topic.index\"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. @layer utilities {
  /*
   * Android 15+ renders installed PWAs edge-to-edge. Paint the app background
   * through the system-bar regions while keeping every app state inside the
   * safe insets, including boot, login, and landscape cutout layouts.
   */
  #root {
    display: flex;
    height: 100dvh;
    flex-direction: column;
    background: var(--background);
    padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
    padding-right: env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px);
    padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px);
    padding-left: env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px);
  }

  /*
   * Shells ask for a full `h-dvh`, which is taller than the inset content box.
   * Let flex shrink them to fit instead of overriding their height: an `auto`
   * height here would resolve every nested `h-full` scroller to its content
   * size and grow the page without end.
   */
  #root > * {
    flex: 1 1 auto;
  }

  .omni-app-text-scale {
    --omni-mobile-ui-font-boost: 0px;
    --omni-mobile-conversation-font-boost: 0px;

## Claude thinking · 2026-10-27T10:43:04.562Z

Since the drawer fills the entire viewport, it overlaps the status bar on edge-to-edge Android PWAs. The fix is to add safe-area padding generically to the SheetContent for left/right sides, covering top, bottom, and the relevant horizontal edge.

But I need to be careful about ordering—since the consumer's className (like `p-0` for mobile nav) comes later in the merge chain, the padding classes need to be placed after `p-0` so they aren't overridden. I'll apply this directly in MobileNavSheetContent's className, ordering it so the environment-inset padding wins over the zero padding, keeping the sheet's own background intact behind the status bar.

Now I should check other right-side sheets in HomeHeader, like the mobile workers drawer and terminal sheet, to see if they need the same treatment.
