## Claude thinking · 2026-10-27T10:43:32.380Z

I notice the terminal and workers full-screen sheets have the same status-bar gap issue, but the user specifically asked about the mobile nav drawer. I'll stay focused on fixing that one, though I could mention the other two share the same bug since it's the same root cause and cheap to fix without really expanding scope.

I'm using safe-area-inset environment variables as Tailwind arbitrary padding values to account for the device's status bar and edges, and adjusting the drawer width calculation to stay within the viewport after adding that padding. Now I'm checking whether the background colors will line up seamlessly in that inset strip, since the sidebar uses a semi-transparent overlay color that's slightly different from the sheet's base background in both light and dark mode.

Rather than padding the sheet itself, I decide it's cleaner to apply the safe-area padding directly on the sidebar root element when in mobile mode, so the sidebar's own background extends into the status bar area without a color mismatch -- same approach for the bottom gesture bar inset and the landscape side cutout. I'm also checking whether the Settings footer near the bottom gesture bar needs its own adjustment.

Now shifting to pin visibility: on desktop the pin button should only appear on hover, so I'm making the PinToggleButton hidden by default and only shown as inline-flex at the lg breakpoint, while on mobile the pin/unpin action should live inside the session row's three-dot menu instead, appearing only below the lg breakpoint.

For remote sessions which currently lack a "..." menu, I need to add one just for mobile so users can still pin/unpin them, since desktop remote rows will rely on the hover button alone. Similarly, local project headers already have a menu I can extend with a pin item (mobile-only), while remote project headers currently show a spacer that I should swap out for a mobile-only "..." trigger.

I'm wondering whether hiding dropdown items with CSS causes keyboard navigation issues on desktop. Actually, there's already a cleaner signal available: ConversationSidebar receives a runnerControlsMode or surface prop distinguishing mobile drawer from desktop sidebar, so I could use that to conditionally render menu items versus hover buttons instead of relying on CSS visibility tricks.

I'm planning to pass a `touch` boolean (derived from runnerControlsMode === "mobile") down into the row components: on touch, pin actions go into a menu item; on desktop, they appear as hover buttons. This applies similarly to the project header and remote rows, and I need to account for how machine labels and other right-side controls (spinner, archive button) are arranged differently on mobile versus desktop.

## Claude · 2026-10-27T10:45:42.110Z

I fixed both. The drawer now leaves room for the status bar, and on mobile, pinning is only in the `…` menu.

**Status bar overlap.** My pin changes didn't cause this; they never touched the drawer frame or its header. The app makes room for the status bar on its main container only. The mobile drawer opens on a separate layer outside that container, so on Android, where the installed app draws under the status bar, it went right up under it. That has been the case since edge-to-edge support was added, so I can't tell why it only showed up now. The sidebar now adds the top and bottom insets itself whenever it's in the mobile drawer, and the gap uses the sidebar's own background colour.

**Pins on mobile vs desktop**
- **Mobile drawer:** no pin icons on rows. "Pin session" / "Unpin session" is the first item in each session's `…` menu, and "Pin project" / "Unpin project" is the first item in each project's `…` menu. Sessions and projects from other servers, which had no `…` menu before, now get one containing just the pin option, so you can still unpin them on your phone.
- **Desktop:** unchanged. The pin icon appears on hover next to the `…`.

**Verification**
- Added a mobile test to `tests/e2e/pinned-items.spec.ts`. It uses a phone-sized viewport and has Chrome pretend there's a 32px status bar and a 24px gesture bar. It confirms the drawer leaves those gaps, rows show no pin buttons, and pin/unpin works from the `…` menus. All three scenarios in the spec pass, and the screenshot above shows the result.
- Typecheck and lint are clean.
- The related unit tests pass, except one failure that was already there before my changes.
- I didn't test on a real phone, so it's worth a quick look once you've rebuilt the app.

Two other full-screen mobile panels, the terminal and the workers view, are built the same way and probably also go under the status bar. I left them alone; say if you want the same fix there.

Nothing is committed.
